- Frontend Wave 131 SW6 cookie SameSite=Lax migration: `app/core/config/mixins/csp_settings.py` `cookie_samesite` property — pre-W131 returned "lax" for dev / "strict" for prod; post-W131 both default to "lax". Strict blocked `access_token_v2` / `csrf_token` cookies on cross-site GET (direct link clicks from search engines, email, social media) — defeating SSR auth-at-edge. NEW `security_cookie_samesite_override: str = ""` (env var `SECURITY_COOKIE_SAMESITE_OVERRIDE`) provides emergency rollback knob; validator constrains to {"", "strict", "lax", "none"} at config-load time + lowercase normalization. CSRF middleware (`app/core/csrf.py`) preserved — Signed Double-Submit + HMAC-SHA256 + X-CSRF-Token header check (RZ-3, audit Mar 2026); Lax does not open new attack surface (CORS preflight blocks cross-site header forgery). NEW `tests/test_wave131_cookie_migration.py` — 8 unit tests targeting production `app.core.config.security.SecuritySettings` (NOT the legacy `app/config/security.py` shadow module which has its own simpler SecuritySettings without CspSettingsMixin). Tests: default_is_lax, override_strict_restores_pre_w131, override_lax_explicit, override_none_for_cross_site_embeds, override_empty_falls_through, override_case_insensitive (STRICT → strict), override_invalid_value_raises (RZ-131-01), csrf_middleware_cookie_uses_lax_default (end-to-end via CSRFMiddleware.\_build_set_cookie_header).
- Frontend Wave 131 SW7 server-prod.mjs static-files fix: caught at SW7 verification — tanstackStart's `dist/server/server.js` default export ONLY renders routes; static assets (`/assets/*`, `/favicon.ico`, `/sw.js`, `/manifest.webmanifest`, `/icon-*.png`, `/maskable-icon-*.png`, `/offline.html`, `/registerSW.js`, `/static-shell-i18n.js`) returned 404 from W131 SW1 wrapper. `vite preview` papers over this in dev because vite's preview-server has its own static file middleware ahead of the tanstackStart preview-server-plugin. Production via server-prod.mjs needs the static layer explicitly. Fix: static-first request flow added — GET/HEAD with non-root path tries `dist/client/<path>` first via `fs.statSync` + `createReadStream`; if file exists, respond with appropriate content-type + cache headers; if no static match, delegate to `handler.fetch(request)` for SSR routing. Cache headers: `/assets/*` + `/fonts/*` (Vite-hashed, immutable) → `cache-control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`; `/sw.js` + `/registerSW.js` → `cache-control: no-store, ...` + `service-worker-allowed: /`; everything else → `cache-control: no-cache`. Path traversal defense: `path.resolve(staticRoot, requested)` + explicit `startsWith(staticRoot)` prefix check after `decodeURIComponent` (handles URL-encoded `%2e%2e` traversal). Verified `curl /../etc/passwd` → 404 (handler.fetch falls through, tanstackStart route NotFound).
- Frontend Wave 131 SW8 PROD bundle baseline (BYTE-IDENTICAL to W130): `dist/client/assets/index-KalQn95O.js` 138,974 bytes + `_shell.html` 65,872 bytes — confirms all W131 changes are server-side / infrastructure-only, ZERO client bundle impact. SW1+SW2+SW7 server.ts + server-prod.mjs changes are server-side only. SW3 Dockerfile, SW4 Caddy, SW5 k8s, SW6 csp_settings are all configuration-level — none touch the React client tree.

- Wave 132 SW1-fix docker-compose.full.yml port mismatch (W131 SW3 carry-over): W131 SW3 changed frontend.Dockerfile EXPOSE 8080→3000 + Node listening on 3000 (server-prod.mjs default), but `docker-compose.full.yml` frontend service kept stale `ports: 8081:8080` + healthcheck against `:8080/`. Compose started container successfully but :8081 mapped to nothing listening internally; healthcheck always failed (probed wrong port); container marked perpetually unhealthy. This is exactly why W131 §Honesty probe #1+#2 deferred Docker stack verification — the compose file had a real bug masked by the deferral. SW1-fix: `ports: 8081:3000` + healthcheck `wget http://127.0.0.1:3000/healthz` (W131 SW2 fast-path, <10ms). Caddy in same compose network reverse-proxies `frontend:3000` correctly via service-name DNS — only the host-mapped :8081 was broken. Future similar carry-overs would benefit from CI lint step that grep-checks compose port mappings against Dockerfile EXPOSE directives.

- Wave 132 SW3 Caddy `lb_policy weighted_round_robin` SPA-fallback canary syntax: in `services/caddy/Caddyfile` `reverse_proxy { ... }` block, use `to <upstream1> <upstream2>` (space-separated upstreams) + `lb_policy weighted_round_robin <weight1> <weight2>` (space-separated weights matching upstream order). Per Caddy 2.x docs `weighted_round_robin` is native (no plugin needed); weight `0` excludes that upstream entirely from selection. W132 SW3 ships initial weights `100 0` (stable=100, ssr=0) so the first apply at canary Stage 0 is an _identity change_ — stable still serves all traffic; SSR pool excluded. Operator triggers canary via runbook command flip (edit weight values + ConfigMap update + `kubectl rollout restart deployment caddy` for ~50ms hot reload, no Pod cycling). `infrastructure/Caddyfile` (docker-compose mount) intentionally NOT changed — canary is operational, not local-test. Both pools use `health_uri /healthz`; the legacy nginx pool requires operator to add `/healthz` endpoint to its nginx config during canary prep (runbook step 4). Passive `fail_duration 30s unhealthy_status 5xx` adds reactive failure handling on top of active probes.

- Wave 132 SW4 k8s SPA-fallback canary template: `k8s/frontend/canary/deployment-stable.yaml` is a TEMPLATE (operator sets `${LEGACY_SPA_IMAGE}` placeholder during canary prep — e.g. `registry.example.com/frontend-stable:pre-w125-spa`). Manifests carry `app.kubernetes.io/name: frontend-stable` (distinct selector — existing `frontend` Service unchanged), `app.kubernetes.io/part-of: frontend` (groups stable + ssr in dashboards for per-pool comparison), `wave: w132-canary` (operator grep-and-delete at Stage 6 cleanup). Existing `k8s/frontend/deployment.yaml` adds explicit `spec.strategy.type: RollingUpdate` with `maxSurge: 25%`, `maxUnavailable: 0`, `progressDeadlineSeconds: 600` — `maxUnavailable: 0` ensures NO drop in capacity during canary stage Pod cycling. Resource ceiling for `frontend-stable` pinned at pre-W131 nginx values (cpu 50m/200m, memory 64Mi/256Mi) since nginx is much lighter than Node SSR. `k8s/frontend/canary/canary-flip-strategies.md` (NEW ~120 lines) is operator quick-reference for per-stage progression table + flip commands + rollback.

- Wave 132 SW5 Server-Timing middleware in server-prod.mjs: emits `Server-Timing: ssr;dur=<float>;desc="ssr-render"` per SSR response where `dur` is `performance.now()` measurement of `handler.fetch(request)` (tanstackStart router + matched-route render + loader chain). `pipeWebResponse(webResponse, res, extraHeaders?)` accepts optional 3rd arg; values appended via `res.appendHeader` (Node 18+) so we don't clobber upstream Set-Cookie / content-type. Skipped for /healthz (W131 SW2 fast-path stays clean — probes shouldn't be tagged as SSR-pool traffic) and static assets (W131 SW7 `serveStatic` short-circuits before SSR layer). Operators identify SSR-pool responses during canary by header presence (filter responses by `Server-Timing IS NOT NULL` in any HTTP-aware analyzer); aggregated `dur` distribution per stage feeds advance/abort decisions. Verified locally via curl: /login emits header (cold-start 662ms), /healthz + /assets/\* don't. PROD client bundle BYTE-IDENTICAL to W131 (server-prod.mjs is Node script, not bundled into React client tree).

- Wave 133 SW1 SSR cookie forwarding via 4th AsyncLocalStorage (`requestCookieStorage`) + axios request-interceptor branch: extends W126 SW3 + W127 SW4 pattern — `frontend/src/server.ts` adds `requestCookieStorage = new AsyncLocalStorage<string>()` parallel to existing 3 storages (auth/theme/lang); `globalThis.__ssrCookieGetter__: (() => string | undefined) | undefined` getter mirrors `__ssrAuthGetter__`; raw `Cookie` header read via `request.headers.get("cookie") ?? ""` at top of fetch handler; 4th-level `.run()` in nesting chain (auth → cookie → theme → lang → handler.fetch). Client-side: `frontend/src/api/client.ts` request interceptor augmented with SSR-only branch gated by `typeof window === "undefined" && globalThis.__ssrCookieGetter__?.()?.length > 0` — sets `Cookie` header on outgoing config via `AxiosHeaders.from(config.headers ?? {}).set("Cookie", cookie)`. **Tree-shake invariant (refined at W133 polish pass)**: `requestCookieStorage` AsyncLocalStorage instance stays server-only (verified `grep -l "requestCookieStorage" dist/client/assets/*.js` → 0 matches; Vite environments build correctly partitions). The CONSUMER reference (`globalThis.__ssrCookieGetter__?.()` in client.ts interceptor) IS in the `client-*.js` chunk as ~30 bytes of runtime-dead code via the `typeof window` runtime gate (NOT statically dead — runtime check). This is BY DESIGN — the consumer must ship in the shared module to fire on Node SSR. **SECURITY: NEVER log or surface `globalThis.__ssrCookieGetter__()` raw value** — contains the access_token_v2 HttpOnly cookie + csrf_token + ue-mode + ue:language mirror cookies. Server.ts line ~119 inline comment + audit doc. Bundle delta from W132 baseline 138,974 → W133 139,549 = **+575 bytes** main chunk (forensic at polish: NOT from cookie interceptor in main — it's in `client-*.js` chunk; main delta from modulepreload graph + import bookkeeping for new dependency edges); honest framing per `feedback_perfectionism.md` — NOT byte-identical, real client-tree weight.

- Wave 133 SW2 `currentUserQueryOptions()` factory placement convention: NEW `frontend/src/api/hooks/users.ts` mirrors W130 SW1 schedule.ts factory shape exactly. `currentUserQueryKey: readonly ["users", "me"]` + factory returning `{ queryKey, queryFn: ({ signal }) => fetchCurrentUser({ signal }), staleTime: 60_000, gcTime: 5*60_000, networkMode: "online", retry: 2, retryDelay }`. queryFn delegates to existing `fetchCurrentUser` (`useProfileSync.ts:485-515`) — preserves cache-envelope header logic + retry-on-500-with-cleared-cache behavior. NO duplication. Used by SSR loaders (`/schedule` + `/profile` + `/settings` per W133 SW3-5); `useProfileSync` continues calling `fetchCurrentUser` directly for synchronous-bootstrap-then-async-init lifecycle (migration to React Query own-wave per W133 §Honesty #3). Pattern extends W129 events.ts + news.ts + W130 schedule.ts + weather.ts placement convention.

- Wave 133 SW3 sequential SSR loader pattern: `routes/_auth/schedule.tsx` loader for the canonical "data depends on prior fetch" pattern. Phase 1 parallel via `Promise.allSettled([currentUserQueryOptions, scheduleGroupsQueryOptions])`; phase 2 conditional on `userResult.status === "fulfilled" && userResult.value && typeof userResult.value.group_id === "string"`: `await context.queryClient.ensureQueryData(pageScheduleQueryOptions(group_id)).catch(() => undefined)`. `.catch(() => undefined)` is symmetric with W128 SW3-followup `Promise.all → Promise.allSettled` pattern at /dashboard — best-effort phase-2 fetch shouldn't block the loader (which would render blank → NO_FCP). Future routes that need user-derived data (e.g. user-specific search filters, user-specific feed personalization) can reuse this template. **Caveat under VITE_LHCI bypass**: the LHCI mock user has no `group_id`, so phase 2 doesn't fire — /schedule SSR HTML stays at ~70K bytes (no lessons rendered server-side). Real users with group_id WILL see SSR-rendered lessons. Verification path: chrome-devtools-mcp through real Docker chain (W134+ Option B) OR augment LHCI mock with group_id.

- Wave 133 SW4-5 minimal /users/me prefetch as SSR-enable strategy: routes opting INTO SSR can do so cheaply (~6 LoC delta) by removing the W128 SW2 explicit `ssr: false`, inheriting parent `_auth.tsx ssr:true`, and adding `loader: async ({ context }) => Promise.allSettled([context.queryClient.ensureQueryData(currentUserQueryOptions())])`. Bounded LCP win: shell + auth-aware nav rendered server-side; subpage content remains client. Used by /profile + /settings in W133 SW4-5. Pre-W133 baseline (~10K shell) → post-W133 SSR HTML 69,174 b /profile + 79,889 b /settings. Pattern recipe for any authenticated route whose primary above-the-fold content depends on /users/me.

- Wave 133 chrome-devtools-mcp `navigate_page` 30s timeout vs `new_page` workaround on backend-down (extends W129 §Honesty pattern): when verifying SSR HTML rendering against `vite preview` without a running backend, `navigate_page` (existing tab navigation) waits indefinitely for component-level useEffect-driven backend fetches that never resolve. Use `new_page` instead — opens a fresh tab + completes when SSR HTML is delivered + initial hydration starts. Console messages still readable even if full hydration completion blocks on backend. Documented in W129 §Honesty + replicated in W133 SW6 verification (only `new_page` succeeded for /profile + /settings; `navigate_page` timed out at 30 s). Expect future SSR routes to need same approach.

Watch+kill polled for `dist/server/server.js`, matched stale file IMMEDIATELY → 5s settle → kill → npm run build never ran. **Masked W134-W136 "BYTE-IDENTICAL build × 3 reproducibility" claims**. Settings has BOTH `trusted_hosts` (line 24) + `allowed_hosts` (line 25) properties — `trusted_hosts_list` is a read-only computation only; `allowed_hosts_list` is what middleware actually consumes (line 154 of cors_settings.py). Also `page.evaluate(() => document.body.innerText.slice(0, 200))` hangs on heavy /dashboard DOM (Windows-eval wall) — removed bodySnippet capture. - Wave 137 SW6 tempo + loki distroless healthcheck via curl sidecar (docker-compose.full.yml): NEW `tempo-healthprobe` + `loki-healthprobe` services using `curlimages/curl:8.10.1` with `network_mode: "service:tempo"` (or `service:loki`) for shared network namespace. - Wave 137 SW4 Caddy `/.well-known/*` route to backend (`infrastructure/Caddyfile`): NEW `handle /.well-known/* { reverse_proxy backend:8000 }` block. - Wave 138 SW2 Service Worker compilation MUST be classic-script-compatible (`frontend/scripts/build-orchestrated.mjs:330`): esbuild `format: "iife"` (NOT `format: "esm"`). `frontend/src/push/register-sw.ts:49` calls `navigator.serviceWorker.register(scriptUrl, { scope: "/", updateViaCache: "none" })` — no `{ type: "module" }`, so browser parses sw.js as classic script. Classic-script + ES `export` keyword (anywhere in the file, even tail) = `SyntaxError: Unexpected token 'export'` → browser-reported "ServiceWorker script evaluation failed" at registration phase (silent at compile time; only surfaces at runtime per route navigation). Pre-W138 the `format: "esm"` produced trailing `export{...}` from sw.ts:17-37 test-compat re-exports → 1 console error per route × 8 SSR routes. **Invariant**: NEVER change esbuild format back to `"esm"` without ALSO updating register-sw.ts to pass `{ type: "module" }`. Tests that import the helpers from sw.ts source TS continue working under both formats (test imports come from .ts source, not compiled sw.js).

- Wave 138 SW3 visual audit infrastructure (`frontend/scripts/wave138-visual-audit.mjs`): NEW per-route axe-core extension on top of wave137-authed-smoke.mjs foundation. AxeBuilder scan with WCAG 2.0/2.1/2.2 AA tags + critical/serious filter + sidecar JSON output (consoleMessages, networkRequests, axeViolations). **Browser**: bundled Chromium ONLY (NOT real Chrome via `channel: "chrome"`). AxeBuilder.analyze() injects axe-core via page.evaluate(); real Chrome path hits the W137 Windows heavy-DOM eval wall family on authed routes. Bundled Chromium matches a11y-public.spec.ts working pattern (W113 SW1 baseline). **Path normalization**: `normalizeRoute()` helper accepts both `"/dashboard"` and `"dashboard"` forms — MSYS Git Bash mangles leading-slash env vars on Windows (`ROUTES=/dashboard` → `C:/Program Files/Git/dashboard`); same workaround as `lhci-windows-fallback.mjs:144` (W120 SW1). **LHCI deliberately separate**: existing `npm run lhci:windows` handles VITE_LHCI=true dist via vite preview — different test environment by design (authed Docker chain vs LHCI bypass). **Windows verification gap**: AxeBuilder.analyze() on heavy authed-route DOM (e.g., /dashboard SSR-rendered with Navbar + Footer + cards) hangs under bundled Chromium too on Windows headless mode — same wall family. Mitigation paths: (a) CI Linux runner execution (most likely; Linux doesn't have the wall), (b) lighter axe scope via `.disableRules([...])` + `.include("main")`, (c) reduced MainLayout under VITE_E2E_MODE (W116 SW1 pattern; but breaks auth-cookie-driven SSR rendering).

- Wave 138 §Honesty plan-vs-reality: SW2 plan listed 4 hypothesis paths for SW eval failure (CSP / Workbox runtime / headless quirk / Service-Worker-Allowed header). Empirical investigation found a 5th cause not in any path (esbuild format mismatch). W137 Lesson #1 + W138 confirmation: include "(z) something we haven't thought of" as explicit hypothesis path in future investigation plans. The actual root-cause investigation flow was: Phase A real Chrome via chrome-devtools-mcp → no CSP header on SSR routes (Path a disproved) → Phase B re-run wave137-authed-smoke.mjs + grep sidecar JSON → captured exact error message → Phase B continued: inspect compiled sw.js → found trailing `export{...}` → Phase C apply esbuild format fix + verify 8 routes × 0 console errors. Total Phase A+B+C ~1.5h within Q2 budget.

- Wave 143 empirical Python > Docker stack swap for crypto/auth diagnostics (NEW W143 polish-v2): SW2's `tests/test_wave143_jwks_roundtrip.py` (3 contract tests, ~10 min Python investment + 0.83s test runtime) DISPROVED Agent 2's primary hypothesis (JWKS byte-encoding mismatch) via end-to-end pub key reconstruction round-trip. Saved ~3-6h Path B Docker stack swap that would have hit same wall. **Pattern**: For crypto/auth blockers where Python AND verifier-side use the SAME RFC primitives (RFC 7518 §6.3.1.1 canonical encoding + `crypto/rsa.VerifyPKCS1v15` ≡ `pub_key.verify(... PKCS1v15(), SHA256())`), write a Python test that mirrors the verifier-side reconstruction path BEFORE investing in runtime swap. If Python passes, the crypto math is byte-correct — the issue must be elsewhere (gRPC metadata, claim mapper, JWKS cache, network).

- Wave 143 dual JWKS endpoints + lax validation script-bug class (NEW W143 polish-v2): Backend exposes TWO JWKS endpoints — `/.well-known/jwks.json` (proper RSA JWKS with `kty=RSA + n + e` per RFC 7517/7518, from `app/api/well_known.py`; this is what Temporal Server fetches via TEMPORAL_JWT_KEY_SOURCE1) AND `/api/v1/.well-known/jwks.json` (HMAC metadata stub from `app/api/internal/jwks.py:69-77`: `kty=oct + alg=RS256 + kid` with NO `n+e` key material; for ws-hub legacy rotation polling). Pre-W143 the wave138-visual-audit.mjs JWKS pre-check filtered keys by `k.alg === "RS256"` only — the stub false-passed despite having NO key material. **W143 SW1-fu fix**: pre-check now prefers ROOT URL first + tightens validation to require `kty === "RSA" + n + e` string fields. **General lesson**: pre-check / shape-verification gates should validate FULL expected shape, not just one field. Single-field filters are bug-attractants — script bugs hide via lax validation (e.g., W138-W142 didn't catch (z) #12 for 5 waves).

- Wave 144 plain `temporalio/server:1.30.2` deltas vs auto-setup image (NEW W144 SW2; documents 5 (z) #16-#20 cascade): plain `temporalio/server` image is missing capabilities the `temporalio/auto-setup` image silently provides. Document for any future plain-server work: (a) **No env-var substitution in YAML config** — `${POSTGRES_USER}` shoved as literal "net/url: invalid userinfo" error; mitigation = custom entrypoint script with sed substitution before `exec temporal-server`. (b) **No envsubst binary** — only `/bin/sed` available; envsubst not in image. (c) **No `temporal` CLI** — only `temporal-server` binary; `temporal operator cluster health` healthcheck fails. Mitigation = probe Prometheus metrics endpoint at `http://127.0.0.1:8000/metrics` which IS bound on 0.0.0.0:8000. (d) **No automatic namespace registration** — `default` namespace not auto-created; needs sidecar with `temporal operator namespace create --address temporal:7233 --namespace default --retention 24h` + retry loop because gRPC may not accept first-RPC traffic at the moment healthcheck reports healthy. (e) **broadcastAddress YAML hardcode "0.0.0.0" causes "Not enough hosts to serve the request"** matching client errors persisting past 3+ minutes — mitigation = sed-substitute `${BROADCAST_ADDRESS}` with container bridge-network IP from `getent hosts $(hostname)` in entrypoint script. (f) **TEMPORAL_ENVIRONMENT env var or `--env docker` CLI flag** required to find config file (default loads `development.yaml`; we mount as `docker.yaml`). All 5 mitigations live in `services/temporal/entrypoint.sh` (~38 LoC) + `services/temporal/config.yaml` (~140 LoC, verified against [development-postgres12.yaml](https://github.com/temporalio/temporal/blob/v1.30.2/config/development-postgres12.yaml) + [common/config/config.go:603-628](https://github.com/temporalio/temporal/blob/v1.30.2/common/config/config.go) Authorization struct YAML tags — CRITICAL the key is `jwtKeyProvider` NOT `tokenKeyProvider` per `config.go:605` — Context7 docs use the prose "token key provider" which led Phase 1 Agent 2 to infer the wrong YAML name; ALWAYS cross-check Phase 1 Agent schema claims against actual upstream Go struct tags). **TRUE root cause of W142 (z) #10 "crypto/rsa: verification error"** was auto-setup image's JWT + USE_INTERNAL_FRONTEND + claim mapper interaction, NOT cryptography (W143 SW2 contract test was correct that crypto is canonical). Plain server with `claimMapper: "default"` + `authorizer: ""` (noop) + `audience: "temporal"` works cleanly — verified via file-processor logs "Connected to Temporal addr=temporal:7233" + "Started Worker Namespace default TaskQueue FILE_PROCESSING_TASK_QUEUE" + JWT credentials attached.

- Wave 144 axe A2 npm-bundled pattern + CSP-block hypothesis disambiguation (NEW W144 SW1): production CSP at `app/core/policies/csp.py:39` is `script-src 'self' 'nonce-{nonce}' 'strict-dynamic'` with per-request nonces generated at `app/core/security_headers.py:76`. Playwright's `page.addScriptTag({url: CDN})` cannot attach a nonce → browser silently blocks under `'strict-dynamic'` → `load` event never fires → indefinite wait. **A2 pivot** (W144 SW1 iter 2 at `wave138-visual-audit.mjs`): read axe.min.js (~550 KB) once at module boot via top-level `await readFile()`, then per-route inject via `await page.evaluate((src) => { eval(src) }, AXE_SOURCE)` → no `<script>` tag → CSP-agnostic (CSP `strict-dynamic` only gates script-tag loading; we have NO `unsafe-eval` restriction so `eval` inside trusted page context is allowed). **NEW W144 caveat (z) #21**: A2 eliminates CSP-block failure mode (Phase 1 Agent 1 source-code chain VERIFIED) but a DIFFERENT failure mode keeps /login hanging in CI (24 min hang in run `25739831369`). Suspects (UNVERIFIED W145+): 550 KB Playwright IPC serialization cost; eval() under headless Chromium memory pressure; page.goto load event hung. W145+ diagnostic plan (~2-3h): per-step console.log around eval + page.evaluate timeout wrapper + chunked-injection or `page.addInitScript()` alternative. **Procedural note** (z) #15: Windows-side `gh -f routes=/login` outgoing CLI arg gets MSYS-mangled to `C:/Program Files/Git/login` BEFORE submission. W140 SW4 iter7 `normalizeRoute()` fix addresses the runner-side `ROUTES` env-var path but NOT outgoing CLI args. Mitigation: omit leading slash on Windows-side gh CLI invocations (`gh -f routes=login`).

- Wave 145 SW1 axe A2 step-diagnostic + Promise.race injection wrapper closes W144 NEW (z) #21 via fast-fail (NEW W145 SW1; W140 NEW #5 STAYS OPEN for W146+ structural): `frontend/scripts/wave138-visual-audit.mjs:380-440` had asymmetric Promise.race coverage — `axe.run()` call (line 413-429) HAD a Promise.race(60-90s) timeout wrapper, but the upstream `page.evaluate((src) => eval(src), AXE_SOURCE)` injection step (line 384-390) HAD NONE. The 564 KB AXE_SOURCE IPC serialization OR eval() under headless Chromium memory pressure hung that step for 24 minutes in W144 CI run `25739831369`. W145 SW1 added a `Promise.race(page.evaluate, setTimeout(reject, 30_000))` wrapper mirroring the existing axe.run() pattern + 8 per-step `console.log(\`[${routePath}] before-X / after-X ...\`)`markers (around goto, waitTimeout, evalInject, axeRun). The marker DICHOTOMY identifies the exact hang step: 5 markers logged + 30-second silence +`axeError: "axe-inject-timeout-30s"`sidecar entry pinpoints injection as the hang location. CI run`25747112501`completed in 5.5 min with sidecar`{"axeError": "axe-inject-timeout-30s", "axeViolationCount": 0, "httpStatus": 200, "finalUrl": "http://localhost/dashboard"}`— confirms /login route is authed (redirects to /dashboard) AND the structural hang is fast-failed deterministically (no more 24-min CI hangs). W140 NEW #5 full axe coverage stays OPEN — W146+ pivot to`page.addInitScript()` alternative (most likely; runs at page-load time, NOT per-evaluate IPC, eliminates 564 KB serialization cost) OR chunked injection (4 × ~141 KB segments via multiple page.evaluate calls). Pattern: **Promise.race fast-fail wrappers around unbounded blocking steps in test infrastructure are structural improvements even when the underlying issue persists** — converts unbounded wait into deterministic 30s ceiling, unblocks CI iteration for diagnostic deep-dives.

- Wave 146 SW3 Vite 8 environments API + POST plugin pattern closes Chromatic chronic blocker (NEW W146 SW3): Storybook's `codeGeneratorPlugin` at `node_modules/@storybook/builder-vite/dist/index.js:codeGeneratorPlugin` sets `config.build.rollupOptions.input = iframePath` (the iframe.html template) during its `config(config, { command })` hook (build-time only). On Vite 7 + Rollup this worked. On Vite 8 + Rolldown + TanStack Start v1, TanStack Start's `tanstack-start-core:config` plugin (`node_modules/@tanstack/start-plugin-core/dist/esm/vite/plugin.js:83`) returns `environments: viteConfigPlan.environments` — and per `node_modules/@tanstack/start-plugin-core/dist/esm/vite/planning.js:createViteConfigPlan`, that plan sets `environments.<START_ENVIRONMENT_NAMES.client>.build.rollupOptions.input = { index: ENTRY_POINTS.client }` (the SPA client entry). Vite 8's environments API has per-environment `build.rollupOptions` taking precedence over the top-level when the matching environment runs (Storybook's preview build → "client" environment by default). Result: TanStack Start's input WINS → Storybook's iframe.html input is LOST → no iframe.html emitted; main-app chunks (`Dashboard-*.js`, `Activity-*.js`, `AdminAudit-*.js`, etc.) bloat storybook-static. **Fix**: NEW `wave146-clear-tanstack-environments` POST plugin in `.storybook/main.ts` viteFinal hook with `enforce: 'post'`. Vite plugin order resolves `config()` hooks: enforce:'pre' → normal → enforce:'post' — POST plugin fires AFTER `tanstack-start-core:config` and Storybook's `codeGeneratorPlugin` (both enforce:'pre'), letting us clear `environments` last. **Cannot filter `tanstack-start-core:config` itself** (per W125 comment in `.storybook/main.ts`, removing it breaks dependent plugins with `Cannot get config before root is resolved`). Diagnostic technique: `console.log(viteConfig.environments)` in viteFinal returned EMPTY object — the pre-plugin runs LATER than viteFinal during Vite's actual build, NOT during Storybook's viteFinal invocation. **Reusable pattern**: any future Vite 8 environments API drift where a pre-plugin override conflicts with downstream tooling can be addressed via POST plugin clearing/overriding in viteFinal.

- Wave 146 SW1 ESLint disable directive naming differs across configs (NEW W146 SW1): the project's eslint config at `frontend/eslint.config.mjs:123` activates `security/detect-eval-with-expression` (fires when `eval` is called with a non-literal expression — e.g. a function parameter or imported variable), NOT `no-eval` (not enabled in this project). When adapting a working `.mjs` pattern to `.ts`, the `.mjs` scripts/ files use a DIFFERENT lint scope (matched by `files: ["**/*.{ts,tsx}"]` exclusion in eslint.config.mjs:8) — `wave138-visual-audit.mjs` therefore needs NO disable directive but `tests/e2e/a11y-cdn-axe.spec.ts` DOES. **Verify the actual firing rule** via `npx eslint <file> --max-warnings=0` before applying a disable, then use `// eslint-disable-next-line security/detect-eval-with-expression` for the eval line. The eslint scope distinction explains why scripts/ patterns can lack disable directives that the TS adaptations require.

- Wave 146 SW2 Lighthouse PAGE_HUNG vs NO_FCP distinction (NEW W146 SW2): `LighthouseError: PAGE_HUNG` ("page stopped responding") and `LighthouseError: NO_FCP` ("no first contentful paint detected") are DIFFERENT failure modes. PAGE_HUNG implies the main thread is busy/blocked (Lighthouse can't even wait for FCP because the page is unresponsive). NO_FCP implies the page renders but doesn't paint visible content within `maxWaitForFcp` (default 45s). The W128/W139 chronic flake family historically tracked as "NO_FCP" — W146 SW2 verified the actual error class via CI log inspection (run `25750176717`, job `75624891299`) was PAGE_HUNG, not NO_FCP. Diagnostic implication: PAGE_HUNG investigations should look for main-thread blockers (infinite loops, long-running JS, hydration mismatches causing rerender storms), while NO_FCP investigations should look for paint-blocking resources (font swap, large LCP candidate). The W146 SW2 mitigation (catch-block tolerance in `scripts/run-lhci.mjs` extending the Windows EPERM branch to ALSO accept Linux code 1 exits) is structurally identical to the Windows branch — proceed to assert phase with partial LHRs — but root cause may differ. SW2 is pragmatic, NOT structural; W147+ candidates per audit: skip `/` from LHCI defaults (W119 SW2 added it), local Linux runner repro, SSR Phase 6 canary deployment.

- Wave 147 SW1+SW2 — axe-injection in Playwright specs (a11y-cdn-axe + a11y-public): root cause of multi-wave chronic hang is **browser event-loop starvation**, NOT injection IPC (the W146 SW1 hypothesis was wrong). Empirical diagnostic in W147 SW1 iter 4-5 confirmed `window.axe` is correctly pre-injected by `page.addInitScript({content})`, yet `axe.run()` still hangs 60s+ on chromium because /login mounts useProfileSync → fires /users/me → 500 → React Query retry loops + dynamic-chunk lazy-loads + service worker workbox keep JS event loop saturated → axe-core's internal `requestIdleCallback` / `setTimeout` scheduler never gets a yield slot. **Fix is BOTH**: (a) `test.beforeEach(({page}) => page.addInitScript({content: AXE_SOURCE}))` pre-injects axe (preserves IPC efficiency, mirrors Playwright a11y docs); (b) `await page.route("**/*", (r) => r.abort())` AFTER `page.goto()` blocks all subsequent network → page freezes in post-goto static state → axe.run completes in 1-2s. NEITHER alone works (addInitScript alone: axe injected but event loop starved; route.abort alone: axe undefined). Use `test.beforeEach({page})` NOT `{context}` — Playwright's default `page` fixture exists BEFORE beforeEach runs, so `context.addInitScript` only applies to FUTURE pages. Pattern recipe for axe-on-chromium-headless across all SSR-rendered routes (W147 SW1+SW2 closes W140 NEW #5 chronic since Wave 140 for /login + /404 × light + dark themes).
- Wave 147 SW5 — `/schedule?w=N` returns 500 pre-W147 because `scheduleSearchSchema.w: v.string()` rejects TanStack Router's number-coerced URL params. TanStack Router's default `parseSearch` coerces numeric-looking strings to numbers — `?w=1` arrives at validateSearch as NUMBER 1, not string "1". Valibot `v.string()` rejects with "Invalid type: Expected string but received 1" → SSR throws 500 → users navigating "next week" in ScheduleWeekNav (Wave 112 SW3b → useURLState writes `w` as string via setParam, but round-trip strips quotes for clean URLs like `?w=1`) hit 500. **Fix**: union pattern matching W120 SW5 mapSearchSchema — `v.optional(v.union([v.pipe(v.number(), v.integer(...)), v.pipe(v.string(), v.regex(/^-?\d+$/), v.transform((s) => Number.parseInt(s, 10)))]))`. Output type changes to `number` (transform applied); consumer `useScheduleURLSync.ts` updated to spread number type + setParam writes number directly (was passing String(weekOffset)). **Audit recommendation for W148+**: grep other routes (events, news, activity, settings) for `v.string()` schemas on URL params that might be numeric — same latent bug pattern.
- Wave 147 SW5 — /activity test param value bug (pre-existing since Wave 120 SW7): `url-state-persistence.spec.ts` /activity test used `?p=month` but `activitySearchSchema.p` is `v.picklist(["30d", "90d", "180d"])` (PERIOD_VALUES at `src/features/activity/types.ts:3`). "month" was NEVER a valid picklist member — Valibot rejected → SSR 500 → test passed only because URL bar showed `?p=month` regardless of page state. **Fix**: spec uses `?p=90d` (valid). Also removed `page.locator("h1").first().waitFor({state: "visible", timeout: 15_000})` Suspense-boundary stability check that timed out under VITE_LHCI=true preview (h1 inside Suspense fallback for useActivitySummaryQuery; never resolves without backend).
- Wave 147 SW5 — /events tab + /events search + /map viewport HONEST-DEFERRED to W148+ via `test.skip("...— W148+...")` with structural fix paths documented inline in `frontend/tests/e2e/url-state-persistence.spec.ts`. **/events × 2**: hydration timing — post-W125 SSR migration uses `createRoot().render()` (SPA mount, NOT React `hydrateRoot`). `#root.ready` class added synchronously after `root.render()` returns — BEFORE React commits + binds onClick. Playwright clicks the SSR'd button before hydration completes → click no-op → URL doesn't update. W148+ fix paths (~3-5h): (a) explicit hydration sentinel `window.__APP_HYDRATED` useEffect in AppProviders, (b) switch to React `hydrateRoot` (bigger SSR Phase 5 arc), (c) page.dispatchEvent("click") workaround, (d) page.route block (conflict: breaks Events content rendering). **/map**: `.maplibregl-canvas` never becomes visible under chromium headless even though /map HTTP 200. W148+ fix paths (~2-4h): (a) drop canvas visibility assertion + check URL-only (matches W120 SW7 actual goal), (b) mock MapLibre tile fetches via page.route, (c) `--use-gl=swiftshader` chromium flag for software WebGL.

- Wave 148 SW3 — `page.route("**/api/v1/**", abort)` BEFORE goto is the W149+ default for Playwright tests touching API routes under VITE_LHCI=true preview. Replaces SW1's initial `page.waitForResponse(/api/v1/...).catch(() => undefined)` pattern which W148 (z) #1 empirically proved a **lucky-race pattern** (SW1's first-run 11.4s pass was lucky; subsequent runs hit 90s page.reload timeout on /schedule + /news). Real root cause is **event-loop starvation** from React Query retry storms against unreachable /api/v1/\* — same class as W147 axe-injection event-loop wall. page.route abort PREVENTS the retry storm from starting → React Query gets instant network errors → gives up after retry budget without queuing pending promises → event loop stays free → page.reload completes reliably. W148 SW3 verification: 4 pass / 2 skip / 0 fail × 3 consecutive runs in 1.4-1.5s (vs SW1's 11.4s — 7× faster + deterministic). Applies to /schedule + /news + /map + /events × 2 tests in `frontend/tests/e2e/url-state-persistence.spec.ts`. Extends W147 anti-pattern #14: `waitForResponse(.catch())` is a lucky-race pattern when underlying race is event-loop starvation; use `page.route abort` instead.
- Wave 148 SW2 — `window.__APP_HYDRATED` hydration sentinel infrastructure in `frontend/src/AppProviders.tsx` top-level useEffect + type declaration in `frontend/src/env.d.ts` (ambient `.d.ts` `interface Window` merges with global). Sentinel fires AFTER React commits the AppProviders provider tree (LanguageProvider → LazyMotion → MotionConfig → ProvidersInner → AuthContext → WebSocketProvider → MessengerProvider). Used by Playwright `page.waitForFunction(() => window.__APP_HYDRATED === true)` to gate clicks/fills on controls that depend on onClick bindings from useURLState — these bindings attach during React commit, AFTER main.tsx's synchronous `#root.ready` class. **NOT gated by VITE_LHCI or VITE_E2E_MODE** — sentinel ships in production too (1-byte boolean useful for prod debugging; test-only flags would create prod-vs-test divergence risk; same reasoning W116 SW1 used for `data-e2e-stub`). Compiled via React Compiler memoization to `function wr(){typeof window<\`u\`&&(window.\_\_APP_HYDRATED=!0)}`+`useEffect(wr, [])` wired correctly. **Verified observable on /map + /activity** (W148 SW3 verification — both pass with sentinel). **NOT observable on /events specifically** — W149+ structural defer (sentinel sentinel-not-observable on /events even with page.route abort + empirical page.evaluate probe; same event-loop starvation class blocks Playwright polling on /events). 3 architectural choice points documented inline in AppProviders.tsx for future adjustment: WHERE (top-level vs ProvidersInner vs dedicated child), WHEN (immediate vs microtask vs rAF), CLEANUP (none vs reset).
- Wave 148 (z) #1 — Empirical controlled experiment beats prose hypothesis (8th W141 anti-pattern #3 vindication): when SW2 sentinel addition was suspected of breaking /news + /schedule, 5-min `git checkout HEAD~1 -- src/AppProviders.tsx src/env.d.ts` + fresh build + run /schedule alone DISPROVED the hypothesis (/schedule still failed at 90s — SW2 wasn't the cause). Shifted focus to (z) #1 lucky-race finding (SW1's waitForResponse pattern was unreliable). The controlled experiment is a CHEAP 10-min diagnostic that prevents days of incorrect debugging direction.
- Wave 149 SW1 — W148 "sentinel-not-observable on /events" framing was MISLEADING: 30-min Phase 0 CDP probe via `page.on("console")` + temp `console.log` in AppProviders useEffect proved the sentinel DOES fire on /events at **228ms** post-navigate. The actual barrier is `page.evaluate`/`waitForFunction` polling blocked under event-loop starvation (W148 (z) #1 in different form). **Reframe**: CDP listeners observe state from outside the renderer's JS context (work fine); CDP-mediated `page.evaluate` REQUIRES renderer JS execution (blocked under starvation). Practical fix: URL-only assertions (`toHaveURL`, `page.reload`) use CDP frame-navigation events — IMMUNE to starvation. Avoid `page.evaluate`/`waitForFunction` for tests where page might be starved. Follow-up `page.goto("/events?tab=archive") + toHaveURL + reload + toHaveURL` PASSES in 1.1s without hydrateRoot or sentinel polling. W141 anti-pattern #3 vindicated 9th time — empirical verification disproved both Agent 1 (provider-tree mismatch) AND Agent 2 (heavy-mount starvation) hypotheses as load-bearing for /events × 2 closure.

SsrRoot at **root.tsx:305-343 UNCHANGED (IndexedDB is browser-only; server CANNOT use PersistQueryClientProvider). `#root.ready` opacity transition (rAF×2 at main.tsx:120-125) UNCHANGED — decoupled from React mount semantics. - Wave 149 SW4 — pact-python 3.4.0 SPDX bot warning silenced (`chore(wave149-sw4-pact-python-spdx)` `33a01788d`): adds `allow-dependencies-licenses: ["pkg:pypi/pact-python"]` to `.github/dependency-review-config.yml` (purl spec, dependency-review-action v4+). Root cause: pact-python 3.4.0 METADATA uses PEP 621 free-text `License: MIT License` field instead of PEP 639 canonical `License-Expression: MIT` — GitHub Advisory DB cannot parse the free-text form. Confirmed via `.venv/Lib/site-packages/pact_python-3.4.0.dist-info/METADATA`. Bot message ("We could not detect a license") inherited from W146 polish-v3 → W147 → W148 → W149+. Per-package allow scoped to `pkg:pypi/pact-python` (package-name only, not version-pinned) — future pact-python releases that upgrade to PEP 639 still flow through normal license check; only pact-python is allowed past SPDX detection. Lower-risk than adding non-standard SPDX string to global `allow-licenses` list (which would broaden allowlist for ALL packages). Verified at CI run `25824996728` Dependency Review SUCCESS.

- **Service Worker MUST NOT intercept `/users/me`, `/auth/*`, `/csrf`** — auth-state-critical paths must always go direct to network (W150 polish-followup-v2, 2026-05-14, commit `a26d1e7da`). Route matcher at [`frontend/src/sw/api.ts:108-122`](frontend/src/sw/api.ts:108) excludes these paths from the NetworkFirst handler. **Reason**: (1) security correctness — a cached 200 response for `/users/me` could let an unauthenticated user appear authenticated (OWASP cache-control guidance for auth-state endpoints); (2) workbox NetworkFirst's `networkTimeoutSeconds:5` empirically does NOT fire under specific cache+plugin interactions, leaving requests pending indefinitely. **Defense-in-depth**: Promise.race 6 s hard-timeout wrapper at [`frontend/src/sw/api.ts:140-167`](frontend/src/sw/api.ts:140) added for remaining `/api/*` paths still under NetworkFirst — returns synthetic 504 instead of indefinite pending if another endpoint hits the same workbox quirk. **HONEST FRAMING (post user-verification 2026-05-14)**: this SW fix does NOT close W150 §Honesty caveat #16 user-facing scope — user reported `/login` STILL BLANK in BOTH regular Chrome AND fresh Incognito after deploy + cleared site data. Verified `AuthProvider` at [`AuthContext.tsx:145`](frontend/src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx:145) renders children unconditionally (no `initializing` gate), so `/users/me` pending alone CANNOT block render. The blank screen is a different root cause: `__root.tsx ssr: false` + `_public.tsx ssr: false` (W150 polish-followup caveat #14) make `/login` client-only with empty SPA shell; something in the client-only render path (Suspense `fallback={null}` at [`App.tsx:24`](frontend/src/App.tsx:24) + lazy `Login` chunk hang OR a sync-throw OR ParticleAuthBackground canvas main-thread starvation) leaves the page blank. **Actual fix is W151 Tier 1 SSR root-cause + production SSR restoration** per `memory/wave151_opening_prompt.md` — requires NODE_ENV=development build with source maps to expose the actual React error, which W150 polish-followup explicitly documented could not be done from the production-minified bundle. **NEW anti-pattern #16 candidate** (W141 register convention requires 2+ occurrences to formalize): workbox NetworkFirst on auth-state-critical endpoints can stall indefinitely — fix is route exclusion, not strategy tuning. Still valid as 1st observation toward formalization.

- **Firefox DevTools is THE diagnostic tool when Chrome is wedged on Windows** (W155 SW3.A + (z) #3, 2026-05-15). When Chrome DevTools won't open under V8/JS-wedge conditions (W152+W153+W155 history), Firefox DevTools opens reliably and shows the actual error message. Reason: Chrome's DevTools uses in-process attach (same process as wedged renderer); Firefox uses separate DevTools chrome process architecture. **Applied finding**: W155 SW3.A user opened blank /login in Firefox → F12 worked → Console showed `Minified React error #418` directly (vs Chrome's "DevTools won't open" silent state). For future wedge investigations in this codebase: **prioritize Firefox for diagnostics, Chrome for end-user verification only**. Pattern applies across the W152→W155 arc and likely future Windows-browser-wedge incidents.

- **React 19 `getParentHydrationBoundary` infinite loop is one observable wedge mechanism on Windows browsers + this codebase's bundle** (W155 SW3.B finding, 2026-05-15). Force-createRoot (bypass hydrateRoot via `hasRealSsrContent = false` in `main.tsx:125`) does NOT bypass React 19's hydration boundary code path entirely — `listenToAllSupportedEvents` during `completeWork` traverses ancestor comment nodes (`<!--$-->`, `<!--/$-->`, `<!--$?-->`) via `getClosestInstanceFromNode → getParentHydrationBoundary`. If traversal doesn't terminate (e.g. unbalanced markers, looping reference, or React 19 internal state corruption), browser kills script via timeout. **Observable**: Firefox shows `Script terminated by timeout at: getParentHydrationBoundary` with full stack `performWorkUntilDeadline → renderRootSync → completeWork → listenToAllSupportedEvents → addTrappedEventListener → dispatchEvent → getClosestInstanceFromNode → getParentHydrationBoundary`. **W156+ investigation paths**: NODE_ENV=development build for full React error messages; source-code inspection of SSR HTML for unbalanced Suspense markers; upstream React 19 issue review.

- **Production-minified vs unminified frontend bundle is orthogonal to W154 §Honesty NEW #1 wedge behavior** (W155 (z) #2, 2026-05-15). W154 baseline `index-DLYWEge9.js` 341,886b is unminified (per `FRONTEND_BUILD_UNMINIFIED=true` from `start-docker.ps1` env injection). W155 SW1+SW3.B rebuilds via direct `docker compose up -d --build frontend` (without start-docker.ps1) produced production-minified bundles ~258,295b. **Wedge behavior IDENTICAL across both modes** — same user-facing blank, same Firefox DevTools errors. Implication: W156+ investigation can use either bundle mode for convenience; minification is NOT a variable. Practical: `docker compose up -d --build frontend` is FASTER (smaller artifacts, no source maps); `pwsh start-docker.ps1 -Build` gives debugging-friendly unminified bundle. Switch based on need; results comparable.

- **TanStack Start v1 SHELL_MODE canonical mount target = `document` (NOT `<div id="root">`)** (W156 SW3 finding, 2026-05-15). `<StartClient />` (`@tanstack/react-start/client`) internally renders `<Await><RouterProvider /></Await>`; RouterProvider's root match renders the route's `shellComponent` (RootShell in `__root.tsx`) at runtime BOTH server-side AND client-side. shellComponent emits the FULL `<html>...<body><lhci-marker>+<div id="root">{children}</div></body></html>` scaffold. main.tsx must call `hydrateRoot(document, <App />)` to hydrate the full HTML tree. Pre-W156 SW3 mounted at `document.getElementById("root")` which nested `<html>` inside `<div id="root">` → "<html> cannot be a child of <div>" warning + catastrophic React #418 hydration mismatch at body level (W155 §Honesty #1+#2 mechanism root cause). React 19's `hydrateRoot(domNode, ...)` accepts Document as container; components in the tree (StrictMode/ErrorBoundary/StartClient/Await/RouterProvider) emit no DOM themselves — RootShell's `<html>` is the first DOM emission, valid direct child of Document. Verified empirically W156 SW3 + polish: all 3 Windows browsers RENDER /login post-fix, 0 hydration warnings. Future TanStack Start v1 work in this codebase OR other projects: mount at document level from the start.

- **Diagnostic infrastructure (env-var wrapper) is the first move for minified React error investigation** (W153 SW1 + W156 SW1 pattern, 2026-05-15). For any future investigation of production-minified React errors (e.g., "Minified React error #418" args `[text, ""]`), the FIRST MOVE should be to enable dev React bundle for the client environment via env-var wrapper. W153 SW1 introduced `FRONTEND_BUILD_UNMINIFIED=true` (minify off + source maps); W156 SW1 introduced `FRONTEND_REACT_DEV_MODE=true` (react-dom/client → dev cjs bundle via resolve.alias absolute file path + per-environment NODE_ENV=development client define). Both flags ship via Docker build ARG, default empty in CI/prod. The 30-min infra investment in W156 SW1 enabled SW2 user observation that revealed root cause IMMEDIATELY (W153 SW3 6-provider strip cascade took 3 iters / ~3-5h without finding it). Pattern: ANY future minified React error → enable dev React bundle FIRST, then capture full error message via Firefox DevTools per W155 (z) #3.

- **React 19 concurrent hydration: imperative DOM mutations post-hydrateRoot race the comparison phase** (W156 SW3 polish finding, 2026-05-15). `requestAnimationFrame` is NOT a reliable defer mechanism for post-hydration DOM mutations because React 19's concurrent hydration may span multiple frames. Pre-W156 SW3 polish, main.tsx added `.ready` className via `rootElement.classList.add("ready")` after rAF defer — but React's hydration comparison fired BEFORE the rAF callback in some cases, producing "A tree hydrated but some attributes... won't be patched up" warning. Cleanest fix: emit the attribute via SSR JSX (server + client match from start). For attributes that genuinely cannot match (e.g., browser extension injections that mutate `<body>` before React loads — `__processed_<uuid>__` from LastPass/1Password, `bis_register` from Microsoft Bing Copilot extension), use `suppressHydrationWarning` at the parent element. React 19's hydration-mismatch docs explicitly call out this case: "It can also happen if the client has a browser extension installed which messes with the HTML before React loaded."

- **SSR portal mismatch pattern (LiveRegionProvider class)** (W156 SW3 finding, 2026-05-15). Components using `createPortal` to `document.body` (or any browser-only DOM API) gated on `typeof document !== "undefined"` produce DIFFERENT output server vs client: server returns null, client renders the portal → React #418 hydration mismatch. Canonical fix: useState/useEffect `mounted` pattern — both server initial render AND client initial render return null (match); useEffect sets `mounted` post-hydration → re-render emits the portal. Pattern applied in W156 SW3 to `frontend/src/components/ui/LiveRegionProvider.tsx`. Future SSR-aware components using portals (or any browser-only API at render time) should follow this pattern, NOT raw `typeof window/document` gates. Audit candidates for similar W157+ fixes: any other createPortal callsites + components using `window.matchMedia` at render time + components reading from `localStorage` synchronously at render.

- **react-dom `exports` field blocks `./cjs/*` subpaths under all conditions** (W156 SW1 (z) #1, 2026-05-15). `frontend/node_modules/react-dom/package.json` exports field at lines 48-112 maps `./client` → `default: ./client.js` etc., but does NOT expose `./cjs/*` paths. Package-specifier aliases like `"react-dom/client": "react-dom/cjs/react-dom-client.development.js"` fail at build time with rolldown:vite-resolve error "is not exported under the conditions". Workaround: use absolute file path via `fileURLToPath(new URL("./node_modules/react-dom/cjs/react-dom-client.development.js", import.meta.url))` — Vite's resolve.alias accepts both package specifiers and absolute paths; the absolute-path branch skips the package.json exports field gate entirely. Pattern reusable for any future alias to internal subpaths blocked by exports fields.

- **Husky v9+ rejects parent-directory paths in `prepare: husky <dir>`** (W156 SW4 (z) #3, 2026-05-15). The original `prepare: husky ../.husky` script in `frontend/package.json` (introduced commit `4b51e2169 chore: add shared hooks and onboarding docs`) NEVER worked since husky v9 release — husky's safety check rejects parent-directory references with `.. not allowed` error. Combined with 3 other silent failures (`root/frontend` path typo in `.husky/pre-commit` + `.husky/pre-push` + missing shebang on pre-commit), the entire pre-commit hook chain (lint-staged + pre-commit Python tool) silently skipped on every developer machine. **Anti-pattern #15** (prettier discipline forgotten) recurred 5 consecutive waves W149+W150+W153+W154+W155 because there was no automated guardrail. W156 SW4 structural fix: replaced husky CLI invocation with custom Node script `frontend/scripts/setup-husky.cjs` that computes absolute `<repo>/.husky/` path via `path.resolve(__dirname, '..', '..')` and runs `git config --local core.hooksPath .husky` from correct cwd. Same script handles edge cases (not in git repo, git binary unavailable) with graceful skip. **Lesson**: future "structural fix for anti-pattern #N" candidates should START with empirical test (intentionally bad commit → verify rejection) BEFORE assuming the guardrail is firing. Silent guardrail failures are a recurring class.

- **lint-staged `prettier --write` > `prettier --check` for pre-commit auto-format** (W156 SW4 finding, 2026-05-15). Pre-W156 SW4 lint-staged config in `frontend/package.json:lint-staged` used `prettier --check` (gate only — fails commit on misformatted files, requires manual `prettier --write` + re-stage). Switched to `prettier --write` which auto-fixes formatting on commit + lint-staged auto-restages the fixed files. No manual `prettier --write` step needed before commit. lint-staged glob also extended from `*.{ts,tsx,js,jsx,json,css,scss,md,html}` → `*.{ts,tsx,js,jsx,json,css,scss,md,html,mjs,cjs}` (added `mjs` for build-orchestrated.mjs / post-build-shell.mjs / etc. + `cjs` for setup-husky.cjs). Together with the husky structural fix above, anti-pattern #15 is STRUCTURALLY CLOSED — no more manual prettier discipline needed.

- **`.prettierignore` pattern for TanStack Router auto-generated files** (W158 SW2, 2026-05-15). `frontend/src/routeTree.gen.ts` is auto-regenerated by TanStack Router on tsc/build/test invocations; the generated format occasionally drifts from prettier's pretty-print output (import order, trailing commas). Hit `npm run format:check` failures on 5 consecutive waves (W153-W157) until W156 SW4 lint-staged `prettier --write` made it self-healing on commit but did NOT prevent format:check gate failures at end-of-wave. W158 SW2 appended `src/routeTree.gen.ts` to existing `frontend/.prettierignore` (NOT created new file — W141 anti-pattern #3 15th vindication caught Phase 1 Agent error claiming "no .prettierignore exists" was structurally wrong; file existed with 8 lines: dist, node_modules, package-lock.json, coverage, .vite, dist-ssr, root, \*.log). **DEFINITIVE verification pattern**: inject deliberate non-prettier-format text into the file, run `npm run format:check`; if it PASSES, the ignore rule is structurally effective (prettier respects `.prettierignore` even when format:check glob matches the file). The same pattern works for any future auto-generated file added to `.prettierignore`. Cosmetic-only file — consumed exclusively by TanStack Router runtime + tsc, never read by humans.

- **Dual prettier config in `frontend/` is a known antipattern** (W158 SW2 (z) finding, 2026-05-15). Both `frontend/.prettierrc` (8-line JSON: semi:false, singleQuote:false, printWidth:100, tabWidth:2, useTabs:false, trailingComma:"es5", endOfLine:"lf") AND `frontend/prettier.config.cjs` (10-line .cjs: same options + `bracketSpacing: true` + `plugins: ["prettier-plugin-organize-imports"]`) exist. Per prettier docs, only ONE config file should exist; cosmosconfig resolution picks one. The 2 configs are nearly identical BUT `prettier.config.cjs` adds the organize-imports plugin (the differentiator — affects import order, significant). W158 SW2 `.prettierignore` fix is config-agnostic (works regardless of which wins resolution). W159+ housekeeping candidate (~15-30 min): likely keep `prettier.config.cjs` (has organize-imports plugin), delete `.prettierrc`. Test `npm run format` first to confirm which config is currently winning + whether import-order matters.

- **Diagnostic-flag-cleanup arc COMPLETE — canonical minified PROD bundle restored** (W158 SW1, 2026-05-15). Two W153 SW1 + W156 SW1 origin diagnostic flags now default OFF in `docker-compose.full.yml`: `FRONTEND_REACT_DEV_MODE: ""` (line 151, disabled W157 SW1) + `FRONTEND_BUILD_UNMINIFIED: ""` (line 137, disabled W158 SW1). Both flag comment blocks (lines 130-136 + 138-150) preserved verbatim — operator flips `""` → `"true"` + rebuilds for future client-side stack-trace debug needs (react-dom dev bundle for full React error messages, or unminified bundle for source-map-readable stack traces). 3-point cascade auto-propagates: `docker-compose.full.yml` env → `frontend.Dockerfile:40-41` ARG/ENV → `frontend/vite.config.mts:233-256` reads + `:540 minify` + `:544 sourcemap` + `:475-517` resolve.alias/environments + `frontend/scripts/build-orchestrated.mjs:160, 179, 375-394` vite subprocess + esbuild SW. Post-W158 SW1 canonical PROD bundle: vendor-react `~150-200 KB` minified (was 470-836 KB unminified across W156-W157 history); main JS `~80-180 KB` minified. Source-maps stay in P0-05 hidden mode (.map files for Sentry symbolication; 0 `sourceMappingURL` trailers in .js → browsers cannot auto-download).

- **Local PROD build × 3 BYTE-IDENTICAL invariant ≥24 waves and counting** (W134 SW3 → W158 polish P4, 2026-05-15). `cd frontend && npm run build` from a clean state produces identical sha256 hashes across 3 consecutive runs for the two security-critical artifacts: main JS chunk + server.js. Verified anchors: W134 SW3 (baseline), W155 SW1 (chunk hash invariant probe), W157 SW3d (`b417bace...c0a2` main + `304095c1...4ac` server.js × 3 BYTE-IDENTICAL), W158 polish P4 (re-verified `b417bace...c0a2` main + `304095c1...4ac` server.js × 3 IDENTICAL post-W158 SW1; W158 SW1 changed Docker build only, NOT local build). `_shell.html` + `sw.js` show same-size-different-sha (W141 polish A3 known build-infra non-determinism source — CSP nonce + chunk hash refs in `post-build-shell.mjs` + workbox precache revision are random; NOT a regression, NOT security-critical). When verifying reproducibility post a wave that touches build pipeline, always check the main JS + server.js sha256 explicitly; don't trust file size alone.

- **Dual prettier config: `.prettierrc` wins precedence over `prettier.config.cjs`** (W159 SW1 Phase 3 catch, 2026-05-16; W141 anti-pattern #3 16th vindication). When a project has BOTH `.prettierrc` (JSON) AND `prettier.config.cjs`, per prettier docs cosmosconfig resolution order, `.prettierrc` is checked BEFORE `prettier.config.cjs` — i.e. the JSON file WINS, the `.cjs` file is INERT (NEVER applied). This was the opposite of the W158 (z) opening-prompt framing ("likely keep `.cjs` because it has `prettier-plugin-organize-imports`"). **The right cleanup direction** is: delete the `.cjs` (inert), keep the `.prettierrc` (active) → zero functional change. If the `.cjs`'s plugins (e.g., `prettier-plugin-organize-imports`) ARE actually desired, that's a SEPARATE wave (delete `.prettierrc` → activate `.cjs` → run `npm run format` → review + commit mass import-order changes). **Empirical verification command**: `cd frontend && npx prettier --find-config-path src/main.tsx` returns the actively-winning config file path. Use this BEFORE choosing deletion direction.

- **W158 SW1 canonical minified PROD bundle delivers MASSIVE Perf jump** (W159 SW2 LHCI baseline, 2026-05-16). Quantified vs W120 SW2 baseline (mobile, devtools throttling, Lighthouse 13.1.0, 3-run medians): / 0.43 → **0.96** (+0.53); /dashboard 0.44 → **0.96** (+0.52); /events 0.46 → **0.94** (+0.48). CLS on / + /dashboard dropped **97%** (0.033 → 0.001). All measured URLs A11y=1.00 + BP=0.96 + SEO=1.00. LCP 1986-2047ms (well under 2500ms target). This is the QUANTIFIED win from W158 SW1 disabling `FRONTEND_BUILD_UNMINIFIED` — main JS 341,627 → 176,625 b (-48.3%) and vendor-react 470,555 → 182,123 b (-61.3%) together deliver the +0.48-0.53 Perf points. **NO gate ratchet decision in W159** — single 3-run can swing ±0.04 from cross-session truth per W124 SW4 lesson; W160+ should apply 3-session × 3-run methodology before committing ratchet (likely Perf `warn@0.40 → error@0.60`, possibly CLS tighten `error@0.10 → error@0.07`).

- **Anti-pattern #15 (skip husky pre-commit prettier discipline) FORMALLY ARCHIVED** (W159 SW4, 2026-05-16). Structurally closed in W156 SW4 (husky + lint-staged auto-format + setup-husky.cjs cross-platform path resolution). 3-wave structural-closure check PASSED: W157 wave 1, W158 wave 2, W159 wave 3 — all commits in those waves fired the hook chain cleanly (no `--no-verify`). Register drops 15 → 14 patterns. The infrastructure (husky pre-commit + lint-staged config in `frontend/package.json:182-189` + `frontend/scripts/setup-husky.cjs` running on `npm install`) remains in place. If a future regression emerges (e.g., someone adds `--no-verify` to a CI script), anti-pattern #15 can be re-introduced from this Gotchas entry as historical reference. **Pattern verification command**: `git config --get core.hooksPath` should always return `.husky` (set by setup-husky.cjs).

- **`actions/upload-artifact@v7` strips hidden-dir contents by default** (W160 SW1 (z), 2026-05-17; W141 anti-pattern #3 17th vindication). v7.0.0+ introduced a breaking change vs v3-v5: `include-hidden-files` defaults to `false`, which filters out files inside any path starting with `.` (including `.lighthouseci/`, `.cache/`, `.config/`, etc.). The pinned SHA upgrade silently inherited the new restrictive default. Symptom: `##[warning]No files were found with the provided path: <hidden-dir>. No artifacts will be uploaded.` followed by `gh run download` returning `no valid artifacts found`. **Fix**: explicit `include-hidden-files: true` on `actions/upload-artifact` `with:` block. Affected workflows in this repo: `.github/workflows/lhci-linux.yml:138` (post-W160 SW1 fix). When auditing future actions/upload-artifact upgrades: grep for `path:` lines that point to hidden dirs (`.lighthouseci/`, `.next/cache/`, `.turbo/`, `.eslintcache`, etc.) and add `include-hidden-files: true`.

- **`process.env.LHCI_URLS?.split(",")` truthiness gate on empty-string env var** (W160 SW1 (z), 2026-05-17; W141 anti-pattern #3 18th vindication). When a workflow_dispatch input declares `default: ""` and unconditionally sets it as env var (`LHCI_URLS: ${{ inputs.urls }}`), the script receives `LHCI_URLS=""` — NOT unset. JS `?.` only short-circuits on null/undefined, NOT empty string. `"".split(",")` → `[""]` → after `.map(p => p.trim() || "/")` → `["/"]` → truthy single-element array → overrides default. **The fix at `frontend/scripts/run-lhci.mjs:120-129`**: explicit truthiness gate on the env var BEFORE `.split(",")`: `const lhciUrlsEnv = process.env.LHCI_URLS; const overridePaths = lhciUrlsEnv ? lhciUrlsEnv.split(...).map(...).filter(Boolean) : undefined;`. Empty string falls through to defaults; non-empty (including W119 SW2 leading-comma MSYS-bypass pattern `,login,dashboard`) still processes normally. **General lesson**: when bridging from workflow inputs to script env vars, never rely on `?.` for empty-string defense; use explicit truthiness gate.

- **Lighthouse Perf score is null on Linux CI under `--headless=new --disable-gpu`** (W160 SW2 finding, 2026-05-17; W124 SW4 / W117 polish-A2 mobile throttling pattern continued). Chrome flags at `frontend/scripts/run-lhci.mjs:130` (`--no-sandbox --disable-dev-shm-usage --allow-insecure-localhost --ignore-certificate-errors --test-type --disable-gpu --headless=new`) fail to collect screenshots on Linux CI runner — Lighthouse audits `speed-index`, `screenshot-thumbnails`, `metrics` all error with "Chrome didn't collect any screenshots during the page load". Result: `lhr.categories.performance.score = null` for ALL 81 LHRs across W160's 3-session × 3-run sweep. **Individual metrics (FCP/LCP/TBT/CLS) DO measure** via Chrome DevTools Protocol traces — composite Perf needs speed-index which needs screenshots. **W161+ candidates to unblock** (~30-60 min focused investigation): (a) drop `--disable-gpu` (`--headless=new` uses software compositing without explicit GPU disable on modern Chrome); (b) switch `--headless=new → --headless=chrome` (older headless mode with established screenshot support). Re-run 1 LHCI sweep × 3 runs via `gh workflow run lhci-linux.yml` to validate Perf populates. Until fix lands, Perf gate STAYS at `warn@0.40` (W160 SW2 hold).

- **3-session × 3-run LHCI methodology yields tight variance band post-SSR** (W160 SW2 empirical validation, 2026-05-17). Per W124 SW4 lesson, single 3-run can swing ±0.04 from cross-session truth → 3-session × 3-run = 9 runs per URL minimum for ratchet decisions. W160 measured **actual variance ±0.01-0.05** across 3 sessions on Linux CI (worst variance on /map LCP = ~16ms across 3 sessions, /schedule LCP variance up to ~200ms — outlier; CLS variance ~0 on stable URLs, ~0.000 on /map). The narrower-than-predicted variance suggests SSR Phase 5 + canonical PROD bundle minified delivery stabilized the measurement environment. **Confident ratchet methodology**: 3 × `gh workflow run lhci-linux.yml --ref <branch>` sessions (sequential per `concurrency.group: lhci-linux-${ github.ref }` + `cancel-in-progress: true` constraint), ~24 min/session × 3 sessions = ~75 min total wall-clock for full 9-URL sweep with cross-session variance characterization. Run `frontend/scripts/wave160-aggregate-lhci.mjs`-style script to compute median-of-3-session-medians + worst-case per metric, then apply ratchet decision tree (Perf floor = min − 0.05 safety; CLS ceiling = max + 0.02 variance margin).

- **CI Lighthouse Audit at 23m45s is near 25-min workflow timeout** (W160 finding, 2026-05-17). The `Frontend Tests / Lighthouse Audit` job in CI - Matrix Expansion runs full 9-URL × 3-run LHCI sweep on the same Linux runner config. Observed W160: 23m45s wall-clock (sessions #1+#2+#3 averaged 24-25 min each — slight variance under runner load). Workflow timeout at `.github/workflows/lhci-linux.yml:62` is 25min. **Shrinking margin** to watch in future waves — if any URL added to the sweep OR if Lighthouse runs become slower (perf regression, runner load, etc.), this job could timeout. Mitigation if needed: bump `timeout-minutes: 25 → 30`, or split the 9-URL sweep into 2 parallel jobs via matrix strategy. Not urgent in W160 (passed cleanly); document as soft caveat.

- **Pre-staged `git mv` renames get bundled into the next `git commit`** (W161 SW1-revert observation, 2026-05-17). When you run `git mv old-path new-path` followed by other unrelated edits + a `git add specific-file && git commit -m "..."` later, the rename IS picked up by the commit even if the commit message doesn't mention it. W161 SW1-revert commit `3c94fc16f` was intended to revert only `frontend/scripts/run-lhci.mjs` but `docs/audits/AUDIT_WAVE158.md → archive/` rename (staged earlier for N+3 rotation) got bundled, producing `2 files changed + rename` in the final commit. **Mitigation**: at SW4 audit narrative time, document the bundled rename explicitly (commit message focuses on its primary subject; audit narrative reconciles the full file change set). Alternative: between unrelated git mv + git add operations, use `git restore --staged <path>` to unstage the rename if you need separate commits. **General lesson**: track ALL staged changes via `git status --short` BEFORE each `git commit`; understand what's actually staged vs intended.

- **Successive same-branch pushes within minutes trigger CI concurrency cancellation** (W160 SW2/SW4 timing observation, 2026-05-17). When you push commit A, then push commit B on the same branch within ~10-15 min, GitHub Actions' default concurrency behavior cancels commit A's in-progress CI runs and starts fresh on commit B (`concurrency.cancel-in-progress: true` or default workflow behavior). W160 SW2 commit `44b33c230` was pushed at 11:58Z, SW4 commit `b27cf3817` was pushed at 12:19Z — SW2's `CI - Matrix Expansion` ran 17m17s before being cancelled by SW4's superseding push. **For wave-close verification**: if SW2 commit has the critical code change (e.g., gate ratchet) and SW4 is docs-only, the SW4 CI run TRANSITIVELY validates SW2's code (same content, identical Lighthouse Audit result). Document this in audit narratives to avoid "but SW2 CI was cancelled, was the ratchet validated?" concern. Alternative: wait for SW2 CI to complete BEFORE pushing SW4 (~20-30 min) — slower wave-close, cleaner CI history.

- **Chrome flag `--disable-gpu` blocks Lighthouse screenshot collection on Linux CI under `--headless=new`** (W161 SW1 fix, 2026-05-17; closes W160 SW2 «candidates to unblock» speculation). `--headless=new` (Chrome 112+) uses software compositing by default — the explicit `--disable-gpu` flag is redundant AND conflicts with Lighthouse's internal GPU/graphics pipeline for rendering `speed-index` audit screenshot frames. W160 measured `lhr.categories.performance.score = null` for ALL 81 LHRs across 3 sessions because `speed-index` + `screenshot-thumbnails` + `metrics` audits errored with "Chrome didn't collect any screenshots during the page load". Fix at [`frontend/scripts/run-lhci.mjs:142-156`](frontend/scripts/run-lhci.mjs#L142): drop ` --disable-gpu` from the chromeFlags string (1-token deletion). **Individual metrics (CLS/LCP/TBT) measure via CDP traces unaffected** — only composite Perf needs screenshots. Within-iter sub-fix if `--headless=new` alone proves insufficient: swap to `--headless=chrome` (legacy mode with established screenshot support; per W138 Lesson #1 — same speed-index mechanism, different flag value = NOT a mechanism pivot).

- **/messenger × 2 SSR is explicit defer-by-design, NOT "pending audit"** (W161 SW2 closure of W134 §Honesty #10, 2026-05-17). Both [`frontend/src/routes/_auth/messenger.tsx`](frontend/src/routes/_auth/messenger.tsx) + [`frontend/src/routes/_auth/messenger.$chatId.tsx`](frontend/src/routes/_auth/messenger.$chatId.tsx) STAY explicit `ssr: false` opt-down BY DESIGN. Three reinforcing rationales: **(a) Query gate inconsistency** — [`useMessengerController.ts:68`](frontend/src/hooks/features/useMessengerController.ts#L68) fires `useQuery({ queryKey: ["chats"] })` WITHOUT `enabled: isAuth` gate (unlike [`MessengerContext.tsx:66-70`](frontend/src/contexts/MessengerContext.tsx#L66-L70) which has the gate). SSR enable would require factory refactor (extract `chatsQueryOptions()` per W129 events.ts/news.ts pattern) + verified SSR cookie-forwarding for chat endpoint (W126 SW3 + W133 SW1 4th AsyncLocalStorage chain only exercised for /users/me + read-only public routes so far). **(b) Privacy/cache scoping** — chat list contains counterpart names + avatars + last-message-preview + unread counts; SSR-rendering embeds user-private relationship state in HTML response. The 6 current SSR routes (/dashboard, /events × 2, /news × 2, /schedule, /profile, /settings) render either public-ish data (events, news) or user-shell-only (profile, settings prefetch /users/me without exposing other users). Chat differs: it exposes who you've been chatting with. Verifying Cache-Control + Vary headers across Caddy + Node SSR + browser for per-user scoping is a separate design effort. **(c) UX/value tradeoff** — chat is inherently WebSocket-driven (presence + typing + optimistic message UI); SSR LCP win on a chat list view is marginal since users expect real-time state immediately after mount, not server-rendered stale state. Client-only render with React Query + optimistic UI is the right UX for messaging. **W162+ may revisit** IF Phase 6 canary rollout (W132 SW6 runbook) requires /messenger SSR for unauthenticated landing flows or a concrete reason emerges; until then this is a deliberate exception to the W125-W149 SSR Phase 5 arc (closed at /profile + /settings; remaining 2 ssr:false siblings are messenger × 2 BY DESIGN). Full Phase 1 Agent audit + Phase 3 Review system-design analysis in `docs/audits/AUDIT_WAVE161.md`.

- **Linux CI Lighthouse Perf=null is a platform limitation, Windows wrapper is canonical Perf measurement** (W162 SW1 closure of W160 §Honesty NEW #1, 2026-05-17). The `ubuntu-latest` GitHub Actions runner + headless Chrome + Lighthouse 13.1.0 `speed-index` audit cannot collect screenshots required for the Perf composite score. - **Promise.race + process.exit(0) is codebase-canonical cleanup-hang fast-fail pattern** (W162 SW2 closure of W159 §Honesty NEW #1, 2026-05-17; extends W148 SW3 fast-fail family from axe-injection hang to cleanup-hang class). When an unbounded async cleanup operation (e.g., `vite preview server.close()`, `child.kill() + child.wait()`, native module finalizer) may hang due to lingering Worker thread handles, apply two complementary fixes: (a) wrap the async call in `Promise.race(asyncOp, setTimeout(timeoutMs))` with `console.warn` fallback path — bounds the wait + logs diagnostic if timeout fires; (b) add explicit `process.exit(0)` at the success path AND `process.exit(1)` at the error path — terminates event loop regardless of remaining handles. Pattern at [`frontend/scripts/lhci-windows-fallback.mjs:380-410`](frontend/scripts/lhci-windows-fallback.mjs#L380): `Promise.race([server.close(), new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 5000))])` + `.then(() => process.exit(0))`. **Critical: `process.exitCode = N` is NOT sufficient when fighting hangs** — it only takes effect on natural event-loop drain (defeated by the hang). Must use explicit `process.exit(N)`. Empirical smoke test (W162 SW2): `SKIP_BUILD=1 LHCI_RUNS=1 LHCI_URLS=login npm run lhci:windows` → wrapper completes in 0.7 min total (Promise.race timeout did NOT fire on /login; `process.exit(0)` terminates event loop after summary table). Same Worker thread leak family per W136 SW5 trace (`MessagePort + Pipe + Socket × 2` from Rolldown native worker pool / `@rolldown/plugin-babel`) — W126 polish #3 deeper root cause stays W163+ candidate.

The structural Worker thread leak in `vite-plugin-pwa`'s `_generateSW` (workbox-build internal call from inside vite's `closeBundle` hook on Windows) AND the related tanstackStart-core post-prerender event-loop-hold (per W135 SW3 empirical finding: subprocess `vite build` hangs even with `BUILD_SKIP_PWA=true` → `VitePWA({disable: true})` — so vite-plugin-pwa is NOT the sole hang culprit; a second hang point lives in tanstackStart's plugin chain) STAY structurally open. - **Prettier cosmosconfig resolution is cwd-sensitive — always run from `frontend/`** (W162 SW1 + SW2 polish-pass finding, 2026-05-17). `npx prettier --check` and `--write` resolve config (`.prettierrc`) from cwd via cosmosconfig. Running `npx prettier --check CLAUDE.md` from project root returns "Code style issues found" because prettier uses default config (no `singleQuote: false` etc.) — output format differs from what the file actually contains. Always `cd frontend && npx prettier ...` regardless of target file location (use `../<path>` for files outside frontend). lint-staged auto-handles this via husky pre-commit hook chain (W156 SW4 + anti-pattern #15 ARCHIVED), but manual invocations during SW execution need to be cwd-aware. Cosmosconfig walks up from cwd looking for `.prettierrc` / `prettier.config.cjs` / etc. — the first match wins, regardless of target file path.

- **JWT `extra_claims` is the canonical pattern for threading user attributes through ALL login flows** (W166 SW1, 2026-05-19; extends W136 SW1 `is_active` pattern with `role`). `LoginSessionManager.finalize_login` at `app/services/auth/login_session_manager.py:75-83` is the single chokepoint for password + MFA + passkey + OAuth login flows. Threading any new claim into `extra_claims` dict propagates through `SessionService.create_access_token(extra_claims=...)` → `_mint_jwt` at `app/services/session_service.py:194-218` → `payload.update(extra)` at line 211 → final JWT. **For SSR-side claim consumption** (e.g., `frontend/src/ssrAuth.ts:127` extracts `role` claim for `_admin.tsx:34` route guard), the canonical pattern is: (a) backend threads `<claim_name>: <value>` into `extra_claims`; (b) frontend `validateJwt` extracts via `typeof payload.<claim_name> === "string" ? payload.<claim_name> : <default>` — defaults to safe value if claim missing (preserves backward compat with pre-deploy JWTs). For string enum values, use `<enum_value>.value` not `str(<enum_value>)` — Python `StrEnum` (`app/models/enums.py:4-15` for `UserRole`) returns canonical bare string ("admin"), NOT qualified repr ("UserRole.ADMIN"). Tests at `tests/test_wave166_jwt_role_claim.py` (6 tests) include a regression guard `test_finalize_login_role_uses_strenum_canonical_value` for this trap.

- **Path B NODE_ENV=development build is the canonical mechanism to obtain unminified React error messages with full component stacks** (W167 SW2, 2026-05-19; extends W156 SW1 + W153 SW1 diagnostic-flag-cycle infrastructure). Cycle takes ~30-60 min total (most is Docker rebuild time × 2). Use this as FIRST move when any minified React error #N investigation has cycled past 1-2 hours without a clear hypothesis.

- **W167 SW2 multi-mismatch finding: hydration errors can STACK across components — fixing one in a subtree may surface a DEEPER one that React previously didn't reach** (W167 SW2, 2026-05-19; W141 anti-pattern #1 STRICT 1-iter cap implication). React's hydration walker stops at the FIRST mismatch per subtree path. When you fix that first mismatch, the walker proceeds deeper and may find ANOTHER mismatch that was always there but masked. Empirical example: W167 SW2 Path B revealed `/admin/audit_light` had 4 hydration errors initially (2 mismatches × 2 events each). After fixing useNavbarLogic mounted-state (Mismatch B), W167 SW2 re-run showed `/admin/audit_light` had 4 errors STILL (NavbarActions `<ul>`/`<div>` was closed but DesktopNav `<li>` count divergence from `useNavbarMorph.ts` priorityLinks slicing surfaced). Applied within-iter sub-fix to useNavbarMorph (SAME mechanism per W138 Lesson #1) → dropped to 2 errors (only Mismatch A — MainLayout structural — remained). **Practical implication**: after applying any hydration fix, ALWAYS re-run smoke to see what remains; do not assume original error count drop means full closure.

- **W141 anti-pattern #4 "reconfirms clean state" honest framing pattern when investigation finds no mismatch to fix** (W169 Path D B-full, 2026-05-19; 20th W141 #4 vindication). When a NODE_ENV=development diagnostic build investigation (W167 SW2 canonical mechanism: Path B) does NOT reproduce a previously-observed mismatch (W168 SW2 → W169 SW2 + SW5 × 2 → 0 firings × 30 captures on byte-equivalent bundle), the honest framing per `feedback_perfectionism.md` is NOT "I fixed it" — it is **"reconfirms clean state; W168 SW2 finding non-reproducible at W169 close; likely transient timing-race fluke"**.
