- **`docker compose` exit code NOT a reliable success signal — cwd drift causes silent failure** (W169 (z) #1, 2026-05-19; W141 anti-pattern #3 37th vindication). Bash command chain `cd frontend && node scripts/...` from a previous invocation persists cwd at `frontend/`. Subsequent `docker compose -f docker-compose.full.yml up -d --build frontend` from that cwd looks for `frontend/docker-compose.full.yml` (doesn't exist) → emits "open ...frontend/docker-compose.full.yml: The system cannot find the file specified" to stderr → returns **exit code 0** (misleading). Background-task notifier reports "completed (exit code 0)". Container state UNCHANGED. Caught only via **independent verification** of container state (`docker ps` Up time matches pre-invocation) + bundle hash inspection (still showing previous build's filename). **Workarounds**: (a) ALWAYS invoke compose from absolute project root: `cd "C:\Users\egorribun\Documents\university_ecosystem" && docker compose -f docker-compose.full.yml ...`; (b) post-invocation, verify container state independently via `docker ps --filter "name=frontend" --format "table {{.Names}}\t{{.Status}}"` — if `Up X seconds` doesn't reflect a recent recreate, the rebuild didn't actually happen; (c) inspect bundle hash via `docker exec ... ls -la /app/dist/client/assets/index-*.js` to confirm new artifact in container; (d) **PREFERRED (W170 SW4)** — use the helper-script wrappers `scripts/dc.sh` (bash) or `scripts/dc.ps1` (PowerShell) which resolve to git repo root via `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` regardless of caller cwd: `bash scripts/dc.sh up -d --build frontend` OR `pwsh scripts/dc.ps1 up -d --build frontend`. Wraps `docker compose -f docker-compose.full.yml ...` transparently. The W141 anti-pattern #3 discipline of independent outcome verification (not trusting agent claims OR bash exit codes alone) caught this silent failure mode in W169 SW4.

- **Docker compose helper scripts at `scripts/dc.sh` + `scripts/dc.ps1`** (W170 SW4, 2026-05-19; structural mitigation for W169 (z) #1). Project-root-resolving wrappers around `docker compose -f docker-compose.full.yml ...`. Both scripts resolve via `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` so caller cwd does NOT influence the resolution — the W169 (z) #1 silent-failure vector is structurally eliminated when the wrapper is used. - **Cross-platform bundle divergence (Local Windows-node vs Docker Linux-node) is a SEPARATE non-determinism axis from W141 polish A3** (W169 polish-v2 A3 finding, 2026-05-19; W141 anti-pattern #3 38th vindication). W141 polish A3 documented SAME-PLATFORM repeat-build non-determinism for `_shell.html` + `sw.js` only (CSP nonce + workbox revision hash variance); main JS + server.js were byte-identical via sha256 in × 2 runs on same machine. W169 polish-v2 A3 surfaces a DIFFERENT non-determinism axis: cross-platform builds (Local Windows-node vs Docker Linux-node `node:24-alpine`) produce DIFFERENT content sha for main JS + server.js (W168 baseline: Local sha `ea956d6d...adf5295` 177,057 b vs Docker sha `d8ef5f60...d3998` 177,057 b — same SIZE, different content). Likely causes: Node.js version differences (Windows local vs node:24-alpine Linux), Rolldown native binary architecture differences (x64-win vs x64-linux), build-time path encoding or locale data differences. **Implication for "BYTE-IDENTICAL invariant" claims**: scope to **LOCAL-MACHINE × N** reproducibility, NOT cross-platform. The ≥33-wave invariant chain through W169 polish-v2 establishes new baseline LOCAL-MACHINE invariant. Cross-platform Docker build produces different bytes but **same observable behavior** (semantic invariant holds — same source code → same React tree → same rendered output). Caught via independent verification (W169 polish-v2 A3 `docker exec ... sha256sum` capture) of audit-doc claim that mis-attributed Docker-vs-local divergence to W141 polish A3.

- **Caddy `handle /ws/*` general rule does NOT include `/ws/ticket` HTTP endpoint** (W173 SW1, 2026-05-20; closes W131 SW4 regression). `/ws/ticket` is an HTTP POST endpoint on backend (issues short-lived OTT for WS upgrade auth per RZ-W14-01 + `app/api/ws/ticket.py`), NOT a WebSocket upgrade endpoint on ws-hub. Caddy `handle` blocks are mutually exclusive + matched in declaration order, so an explicit `handle /ws/ticket { reverse_proxy gateway:8080 }` MUST precede the general `handle /ws/* { reverse_proxy ws-hub:8081 }` rule. Without this exception, POST /ws/ticket falls into the general rule and gets routed to ws-hub:8081 (a Go WS service with NO HTTP `/ticket` route) → 404 Not Found → ALL chat/messenger functionality broken. **Pre-W173 dormancy ≥17 waves** because /messenger was Phase 5 explicitly punted (per W125 design + W134 §Honesty #10 + W161 SW2 explicit defer), so no LHCI/visual-audit/Playwright/axe/e2e regression test exercised chat WS flow. Discovered via real user manual testing (browser DevTools console showed `POST http://localhost/ws/ticket 404` × repeated retries from `useChatWebSocket.ts:222`). Empirical verification: `curl POST http://localhost/ws/ticket` pre→post 404 → 403 (CSRF rejected = endpoint reachable via gateway; matches direct backend test `curl :8000/ws/ticket → 403`). Same exception-routing pattern as W137 SW4 `/.well-known/*` (which similarly precedes default).

- **Node SSR runtime `server-prod.mjs` CONTENT_TYPES map MUST include `.wasm: application/wasm`** (W173 SW1, 2026-05-20; closes W131 SW7 regression). Browser `WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming()` strict-requires the exact MIME type `application/wasm` per MDN/WebAssembly spec; falling back to `application/octet-stream` (the default in `frontend/scripts/server-prod.mjs:116` for any extension not in the Object.freeze CONTENT_TYPES map) makes browsers refuse compilation with `TypeError: Failed to execute 'compile' on 'WebAssembly': Incorrect response MIME type. Expected 'application/wasm'`. Affected modules: `frontend/src/workers/crypto.worker.ts` (E2E encryption via `uni_wasm_crypto`) + `frontend/src/utils/sanitize.ts` (ammonia HTML sanitization via `wasm_sanitizer`). Both have regex fallback per RZ-24-04 design, which is why no visible breakage in non-chat features pre-W173. Crypto worker breakage was only visible in DevTools console + only when chat tries to initialize. **Pre-W173 dormancy ≥17 waves** same root cause as Caddy /ws/ticket gotcha — /messenger Phase 5 punt hid the only feature exercising WASM modules. Empirical verification: `curl -I /assets/uni_wasm_crypto_bg-<hash>.wasm` pre→post `application/octet-stream` → `application/wasm` (size 43,372b identical; only headers changed).

- **Frontend `/ws/chat` ≠ ws-hub canonical `/ws` path — requires Caddy rewrite** (W173 polish-v1, 2026-05-20; closes the second half of chat WS flow chain). Frontend `useChatWebSocket.ts:202` constructs WS URL as `${wsProtocol}//${window.location.host}/ws/chat`, but ws-hub Go service serves WS upgrade at plain `/ws` per `services/ws-hub/main.go:133 http.Handle("/ws", ...)`. Go's `net/http.Handle("/ws", ...)` matches ONLY the exact path `/ws` (would require trailing-slash `Handle("/ws/", ...)` to match `/ws/chat` via prefix). ws-hub `handlers.go:102` explicitly documents canonical URL as `wss://host/ws?ticket=<ott>`. Caddy `handle /ws/chat* { rewrite * /ws; reverse_proxy ws-hub:8081 }` placed BEFORE general `/ws/*` rule transforms `/ws/chat?ticket=X` → `/ws?ticket=X` before proxying — preserves frontend URL semantics + matches ws-hub's documented canonical path. Pre-W173-polish-v1: /ws/chat → ws-hub 404 (path mismatch) → WS upgrade failed in browser console as `WebSocket connection to 'ws://localhost/ws/chat?ticket=<hex>' failed`. Same dormancy ≥17 waves as W173 SW1 fixes — discovered when SW1 Fix B unmasked downstream failure (W138 Lesson #2 stacking phenomenon). Empirical verification: `curl /ws/chat?ticket=test via Caddy` pre→post 404 → 401 (auth firing = endpoint reached; matches direct ws-hub `:8083/ws?ticket=test → 401`).

- **ws-hub docker-compose MUST set `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` env for production-like deploys via Caddy** (W173 polish-v3, 2026-05-20; closes the third ws-hub infra config gap). ws-hub `pkg/config/config.go:103` defaults `AllowedOrigins` to `["http://localhost:3000", "http://localhost:5173"]` — both Vite dev server ports. Production-like Docker setup accesses frontend via `http://localhost` (port 80, via Caddy reverse proxy) → browser sends `Origin: http://localhost` (no port; default :80) → gorilla/websocket Upgrader `CheckOrigin` callback at `pkg/hub/handlers.go:40` rejects mismatch → 403 Forbidden on WS upgrade. Pre-polish-v3 dormant ≥17 waves (same arc as polish-v1 fixes — /messenger Phase 5 punt hid chat WS flow). Fix: add `ALLOWED_ORIGINS: "http://localhost,http://localhost:8081,http://localhost:3000,http://localhost:5173"` to ws-hub env block (covers Caddy canonical + direct frontend port + Vite dev parity). Empirical verification: with all 3 polish iters applied + real 64-char hex ticket pre-written to Redis DB 0 + `Origin: http://localhost` header, ws-hub returns `HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols` (full WS handshake complete; was 403 pre-polish-v3, 401 pre-polish-v1, 404 pre-W173 SW1). Production K8s deployments must set `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` to production frontend hostname.

- **ws-hub docker-compose MUST set `REDIS_PASSWORD` env** (W173 polish-v1, 2026-05-20; closes ws-hub OTT validation chain). ws-hub reads `REDIS_URL` + `REDIS_PASSWORD` per `services/ws-hub/pkg/config/config.go:120-121` (defaults: addr `redis:6379`, password `""`). Pre-W173-polish-v1, `docker-compose.full.yml` ws-hub service env did NOT set `REDIS_PASSWORD` — ws-hub connected to Redis without auth → `NOAUTH Authentication required` startup error → fell back to "L2 Cache disabled" mode → `pkg/hub/handlers.go:195 redisClient.GetDel(ctx, "ott:ws:"+ticket).Result()` for OTT validation returned error → ALL real tickets received 401 at WS upgrade even when ticket WAS in Redis (because ws-hub couldn't read it). Fix: add `REDIS_URL: "redis:6379"` (explicit) + `REDIS_PASSWORD: ${REDIS_PASSWORD}` to ws-hub environment block in compose. Post-fix ws-hub log: `Redis connected (L2 Cache enabled), addr: redis:6379` (was `Redis connection failed, continuing without L2 cache, err: NOAUTH Authentication required`). Same root cause class as W170 SW4 helper-script enforcement gap — config gaps in ad-hoc compose service env across W131 multi-service split arc.

- **TanStack Router context staleness post-W152 Phase 1.7 — route guards MUST read live Zustand state** (W174 SW1, 2026-05-20; closes user-reported login redirect bug + in-app navigation bounce-back). TanStack Router's `beforeLoad({ context })` reads the immutable context object passed at `createRouter()` call time. Pre-W152 Phase 1.7, App.tsx had `<RouterProvider router={router} context={useAuth()}>` — the reactive `context` prop meant RouterProvider re-rendered with fresh context every time `useAuth()` returned a new value. After W152 Phase 1.7 switched to `return <StartClient />` (which internally invokes `hydrateStart() → <Await><RouterProvider /></Await>` WITHOUT a reactive context prop subscribing to useAuth()), the router context became permanently stuck at `DEFAULT_AUTH = { isAuth: false, user: null, loading: false }` on the client. Route guards' `context.auth.isAuth` permanently `false` → every client-side `navigate()` post-login re-evaluated `beforeLoad` against stale context → redirect back to /login. **Fix**: route guards (`_auth.tsx`, `_public.tsx`, `_admin.tsx`) read directly from Zustand via `useAuthStore.getState().{user, loading}` — plain JS call safe in `beforeLoad` (runs outside React render phase). Zustand IS the source of truth — `useProfileSync.ts:1099-1109` syncs internal state INTO it via `useAuthStore.setState({ user, loading, ... })` on every update. Why reload appeared to work pre-W174: TanStack Router's initial-hydration-from-SSR-stream path doesn't re-fire `beforeLoad` for the SSR-matched route — it trusts the server's match result. Server-side `globalThis.__ssrAuthGetter__` (W126 SW4) returns real auth. Only post-mount client `navigate()` calls re-evaluated beforeLoad against stale singleton. `router.ts:31-33` comment was OUT OF DATE post-W152 Phase 1.7 (referenced removed `<RouterProvider context={...}>`).

- **PWA manifest source-of-truth at `frontend/public/manifest.source.json`** (W174 SW3, 2026-05-20). `frontend/scripts/generate-manifests.mjs:14-54` mergeManifests pipeline generates BOTH `manifest.webmanifest` (default locale) + `manifest.<locale>.webmanifest` from the canonical source. Editing only the generated files fails CI `--check` mode at `generate-manifests.mjs:90-100` which asserts no drift between source and generated outputs. Always edit `manifest.source.json` + run `npm run generate:manifests` to regenerate. PWA `screenshots` array (declared on install-prompt UI hints per W3C spec) is OPTIONAL — declarations without corresponding image files in `frontend/public/screenshots/` produce browser DevTools 404 errors + manifest icon download warnings. W174 SW3 removed orphan `/screenshots/schedule-wide.png` + `/screenshots/schedule-narrow.png` declarations after `screenshots/` directory verified to contain only `.gitkeep`.

- **`--text-on-footer` semantic token = constant white in BOTH themes** (W175 SW1, 2026-05-20). Footer is theme-agnostic always-dark — blue gradient in light theme (`--bg-footer-light` via primary-main/primary-hover linear-gradient with blue-400 radial overlay) and nav-dark gradient in dark theme (`--bg-footer-dark` = `--grad-nav-dark`). The standard `--text-inverse` token (white in light / slate-950 in dark) would resolve to BLACK text on dark blue gradient in dark mode = BAD contrast. NEW token `--text-on-footer: var(--color-white)` in BOTH `:root` + `.dark` blocks of `frontend/src/styles/tokens/semantics.css` communicates intent "constant white on always-dark surface". Pattern recipe for other always-dark UI elements (e.g., notification badges with persistent brand fill, sticky banners). Different concept from `bg-brand text-[var(--text-inverse)]` (W116 SW3 pattern) which IS theme-inverted because brand color flips between blue-600 (light) and sky-400 (dark). `frontend/src/components/layout/Footer.tsx` + `footer-link-premium` utility in `tailwind.css` both reference the new token. `min-height: 2.75rem` + `inline-flex + align-items: center` on footer links for WCAG 2.5.8 touch target (was ~20px inline-block); `:focus-visible` via `--focus-ring-isolated` (double-ring per W121 SW5 — needed because solid brand color has insufficient contrast on blue-gradient surface); motion tokens (`var(--motion-duration-fast)` + `var(--ease-premium)`) replace hardcoded `transition: all 0.2s ease`.

- **Frontend CSRF cookie auto-acquisition via axios request interceptor** (W174 SW2, 2026-05-20). Axios's built-in XSRF mechanism in `frontend/src/api/client.ts:66-67` (`xsrfCookieName: "csrf_token"` + `xsrfHeaderName: "X-CSRF-Token"`) reads the cookie + sets the header on outgoing requests. If the cookie is MISSING — first-time visitor OR real user whose `csrf_token` cookie expired (backend's `app/core/csrf.py:71` sets `Max-Age=1800` = 30 min) — axios sends no header, and `CSRFMiddleware` (`app/core/middleware/setup.py:47-60`, NOT in `exempt_prefixes`) rejects with 403 "Несоответствие CSRF-токена" + the `application/problem+json` error doesn't surface as user-friendly UX. Pre-W174 SW2 the frontend had ZERO proactive CSRF acquisition — real users only succeeded when they had a persistent `csrf_token` cookie from a prior session. Backend exposes `GET /api/v1/auth/csrf-cookie` which idempotently sets the cookie; `.github/workflows/visual-audit.yml` (W140 SW4) already ran this dance for CI register flow but production frontend never did. **Fix**: `ensureCsrfCookie()` helper at `client.ts:147-176` called from the request interceptor before POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE. Guards: SSR no-op (`typeof document === "undefined"`); test-env skip (`import.meta.env.MODE === "test"` — Vite literal substitution tree-shakes from prod AND prevents MSW unhandled-request pollution in vitest); already-have-cookie short-circuit (`document.cookie.includes("csrf_token=")`); in-flight singleton Promise dedupes concurrent unsafe requests; `.finally` resets singleton; recursion-guard skips `/auth/csrf-cookie` itself. Empirical verification (W174 SW4): fresh chrome-devtools context with no prior cookies → POST /auth/login no longer 403; sequence is `GET /api/v1/auth/csrf-cookie → 200 + Set-Cookie csrf_token=... → POST /api/v1/auth/login → 200 → redirect to /dashboard`.

- **`useRouteType.hideFooter` is the single source of truth for footer-hiding logic** (W176 SW1, 2026-05-21). Covers `/map`, `/schedule`, `/messenger` via NEW `HIDE_FOOTER_PREFIXES` const array in `frontend/src/hooks/useRouteType.ts`. Combined with `isCompactPage` (login/register/forgot-password/reset-password), MainLayout gates Footer mount via `!isCompactPage && !hideFooter && !E2E_MODE`. Footer.tsx pre-W176 maintained its OWN `isAuthPage = ["/login", "/register", "/forgot-password", "/messenger"]` array (subtly different — missed `/reset-password` covered separately by `isCompactPage`; `hideFooter` missed `/messenger` covered by Footer's check). Both gates together produced correct behavior end-to-end but were duplicated + drift-prone. W176 SW1 consolidated: added `/messenger` to `useRouteType.hideFooter` + removed `isAuthPage` short-circuit from Footer.tsx (also drops `useRouterState` subscription — one less subscription per Footer render). Footer.tsx is now a "trust the parent" component: it always renders when mounted. To add a new footer-hidden route: edit `HIDE_FOOTER_PREFIXES` const ONLY (single edit, no Footer.tsx touch).

- **`FooterBackdrop` ambient orb layer** (W176 SW2, 2026-05-21). NEW `frontend/src/components/layout/FooterBackdrop.tsx` (~91 LOC) — 3 decorative radial-gradient orbs (primary sky glow top-center, secondary indigo accent right side, tertiary white sheen bottom-left) layered above the W175 SW1 `bg-footer` premium blue gradient (light) / nav-dark gradient (dark). Mirrors `EventsBackdrop` architectural pattern EXACTLY — `prefersReducedMotion?: boolean` prop drops `filter: blur(...)` to save mobile GPU; `isNarrow?: boolean` (sub-`breakpoints.content` = 900px viewports) scales orb dimensions down + spreads primary glow wider for better fill; `aria-hidden + pointer-events-none + -z-1 + absolute inset-0` for pure decoration. **Pixel-anchored sizing (W118 SW3 CLS-118-03 lesson preserved)**: orb `width/height/top/left/right` use FIXED PX values (not `%`) — %-based sizing scales with container content growth, contributing to CLS shifts; fixed-px stays stable. Tertiary sheen orb specifically top-anchored (`top: 300px`) NOT bottom-anchored — bottom-anchored values shift when footer copyright wraps to extra lines. Tokens in `frontend/src/styles/tokens/semantics.css` (`:root` + `.dark`): `--footer-orb-{primary,secondary,sheen}` + `--footer-accent-line` gradient (used by `footer-accent-stripe` utility in SW3). Light theme uses sky-300 / indigo-200 / white 14% color-mix; dark theme uses sky-400 / indigo-400 / white 10% (brighter to register on nav-dark base).

- **`footer-stagger-item` Tailwind v4 `@starting-style` utility — distinct from shared `.stagger-item`** (W176 SW3, 2026-05-21). NEW `@utility footer-stagger-item` in `frontend/src/styles/tailwind.css` for per-column entrance stagger. Uses `@starting-style { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(0.5rem); }` — fires AUTOMATICALLY on element mount (no IntersectionObserver needed). Per-element index via inline `style={{ "--stagger-i": N }}` CSS variable; cascade delay `calc(var(--stagger-i) * 80ms)` → 0ms / 80ms / 160ms for Footer's 3 columns. Honors `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` via nested `@media` block. **CRITICAL DISTINCTION from shared `.stagger-item`** (defined in `_micro-interactions.css:188-260`): the shared utility uses `--stagger-i` variable BUT REQUIRES `data-visible="true"` attribute (IntersectionObserver-driven) to transition from `opacity: 0` baseline to `opacity: 1`. Without `data-visible="true"`, content stays invisible. For footer (always in viewport when mounted), IntersectionObserver overhead is wasteful — `@starting-style` fires on mount directly. Don't confuse the two utilities. Variable name `--stagger-i` matches; behavior differs.

- **`footer-social-btn` utility replaces `<Button variant="glass" size="icon">` for footer-specific icon buttons** (W176 SW3, 2026-05-21). NEW `@utility footer-social-btn` in `frontend/src/styles/tailwind.css` for Telegram + Email social buttons. Glass + backdrop-blur on the footer's already-dark surface reads as invisible (glass-on-glass = no contrast). This utility uses white-tinted overlay (`color-mix(white 10%)` background + `color-mix(white 18%)` border) for clear edge on both light blue gradient + dark nav-dark gradient. Preserves WCAG 2.5.8 44px touch target (`width: 2.75rem; height: 2.75rem`) + `--focus-ring-isolated` focus ring (W121 SW5) + hover lift (`translateY(-1px)`) + reduced-motion guard. Footer.tsx uses plain `<a className="footer-social-btn">` instead of `<Button variant="glass" size="icon" as="a">`: simpler, more explicit, drops Button dependency for footer specifically. Pattern reusable for other always-dark surfaces where glass overlay is invisible.

- **TanStack Router `data-status="active"` is canonical, NOT `activeProps`** (W176 SW4 + Context7 finding, 2026-05-21). TanStack Router's `<Link>` AUTOMATICALLY applies `data-status="active"` HTML attribute to the matching link element when its `to` prop matches current pathname (built-in API per [TanStack Router docs `data-status` attribute section](https://github.com/tanstack/router/blob/main/docs/router/guide/navigation.md#the-data-status-attribute)). Using `activeProps={{ "data-active": "true" }}` is **unnecessary and verbose** — CSS selector `&[data-status="active"]` works directly. For prefix-match active state (e.g., `/news` active on `/news/article-123`, like GitHub/Vercel/Linear footers), use `activeOptions={{ exact: false }}` const (single shared `ACTIVE_OPTIONS` object passed to all Links). W176 SW4 implementation: `frontend/src/components/layout/Footer.tsx` extracts `const ACTIVE_OPTIONS = { exact: false } as const` + passes `activeOptions={ACTIVE_OPTIONS}` to each `<Link>` (7 occurrences); CSS selector `&[data-status="active"]::before` in `@utility footer-link-premium` paints 4px white dot. Pattern recipe for any future active-route indicators in this codebase.

- **Login.tsx W177 SW1 reactive useEffect — closes authed-user-on-/login edge case** (W177 SW1, 2026-05-21). `frontend/src/pages/Login.tsx` mounts a reactive `useEffect(() => { if (user) navigate({to:"/dashboard", replace:true}) }, [user, navigate])` watching `useAuthStore.user`. Closes W174 §Honesty #3: authed user who hard-navigates to `/login` (from bookmark / search engine / external link / new tab) stays on `/login` without this reactive trigger, because `_public.tsx beforeLoad` reads `useAuthStore.getState()` ONCE on initial route mount when `loading:true` (per useAuthStore.ts:22-26 initial state — optimistically true until useProfileSync mounts) and returns without redirect → Login.tsx renders → useProfileSync settles GET /users/me → setUser populates store → no reactive trigger re-evaluates the route. **`replace:true` rationale**: prevents `/login` from appearing in back-button history for authed users (semantically correct — authed users should never see /login in history). **Race-safe with useLoginFlow.ts:129 imperative navigate**: when post-login flow fires `setUser(data.user)` at useAuthApi.ts:168 then `navigate({to: redirectPath, replace:true})` at useLoginFlow.ts:129, this useEffect ALSO fires (user transitioned null → set). Both navigates target same destination with replace; idempotent. **W175 SW10 attempted same mechanism but reverted**: msw test infra mocked `/users/me → testUser` globally (handlers.ts:373) → useEffect fired in 7 unrelated tests mounting Login.tsx → form assertions failed → reverted per W141 anti-pattern #1 STRICT 1-iter cap. W177 ships the same useEffect PLUS the msw scoping discipline that W175 SW10 lacked → DIFFERENT mechanism per W138 Lesson #1 → honest new wave with new plan. See `renderLogin({ skipMeOverride })` test helper pattern below.

- **`renderLogin({ skipMeOverride })` test helper pattern + `afterEach` useAuthStore reset** (W177 SW2, 2026-05-21). `frontend/src/pages/__tests__/Login.test.tsx renderLogin()` helper accepts `RenderLoginOptions = { skipMeOverride?: boolean }`. Default behavior (skipMeOverride: false): the helper prepends `server.use(http.get("*/users/me", () => HttpResponse.json(null, {status:401})))` BEFORE `renderWithRouter` mounts AuthProvider — blocks the W177 SW1 useEffect from firing mid-test for tests that verify Login UI form behavior. Set `skipMeOverride: true` for the dedicated W174 §Honesty #3 regression test (W177 SW2 NEW: `"redirects authed user away from /login (W174 §Honesty #3, W177 SW1)"`) — opts out → default msw returns testUser → useProfileSync populates store → useEffect fires → extraRoutes' /dashboard "Welcome!" rendered. **CRITICAL `afterEach` reset**: `useAuthStore.setState({user: null, loading: true, pendingMfa: null, authOperation: false})` clears the auth store between tests in the file. Pre-W177 the auth store persistence across tests was silent because Login.tsx didn't react to user state; W177 SW1 useEffect makes prior-test user-state pollution observable — without this reset, test #2 successful login sets user=testUser → test #3+ mounts Login → useEffect fires immediately on mount → form inputs gone → all subsequent tests fail. Test-file-local reset chosen over `setupTests.ts` global reset to minimize blast radius. W178+ candidate: global reset if similar issue surfaces in other test files.

- **`_public.tsx` layout-level reactive redirect for authed users — closes W177 §Honesty #2 across all 5 public routes** (W178 SW1, 2026-05-21). `frontend/src/routes/_public.tsx` now exports a named `PublicLayout` function with a reactive `useEffect(() => { if (user) navigate({to:"/dashboard", replace:true}) }, [user, navigate])` watching `useAuthStore.user`. Covers ALL 5 routes under `/_public/` (`/login` + `/forgot-password` + `/register` + `/reset-password` + `/reset-password/$token`) via single mechanism, parallel to W177 SW1's Login.tsx-specific useEffect. **Defense-in-depth with Login.tsx**: both useEffects fire when user transition null→set occurs on /login; React 19 child-effect-before-parent-effect ordering means Login.tsx fires first, then PublicLayout would fire — but second navigate is no-op once route changed. Removing Login.tsx's would orphan the W177 §Honesty #3 regression test + break Login.test.tsx. **beforeLoad-vs-useEffect division of labor**: W174 SW1 `beforeLoad` reads `useAuthStore.getState()` ONCE on initial route mount (synchronous redirect throw if user already set); W178 useEffect catches subsequent transitions that beforeLoad cannot see — e.g. authed user opens /forgot-password via bookmark when loading:true → beforeLoad returns without redirect → PublicLayout mounts → useProfileSync settles /users/me → setUser populates store → useEffect observes transition → redirect. **Hardcoded /dashboard target** matches W177 SW1 (preserving `state.from` / `search.redirect` is W177 §Honesty #3 / Q0 option C, out of W178 scope). **Named export** required for the dedicated unit test at `routes/__tests__/_public.test.tsx` to mount it under a custom route tree (createRoute + addChildren) — `renderWithRouter` helper builds flat tree + does NOT exercise layout components per its docstring caveat lines 50-54. The custom-tree pattern is reusable for future layout-level testing.

- **TanStack Router `routeFileIgnorePattern` is REGEX not GLOB** (W178 SW1 (z) #1, 2026-05-21). `tanstackStart({ router: { routeFileIgnorePattern: "..." } })` in `frontend/vite.config.mts` passes the value to `new RegExp(...)` in `@tanstack/router-generator/dist/esm/generator.js:127`. Despite the build-time warning text suggesting glob-like syntax ("Use 'routeFileIgnorePattern' in your config to match this file"), the value is NOT a glob — `"**/__tests__/**"` throws `Invalid regular expression: /\*\*/__tests__/\*\*/g: Nothing to repeat` because `**` isn't a valid regex token (`*` requires a preceding atom). Fix: use a bare path substring like `"__tests__"` (matches any path containing `/__tests__/`). Empirically caught at first rebuild attempt + documented inline in vite.config.mts comment block. W141 anti-pattern #3 39th vindication — empirical test caught Agent-style assumption from warning text. Pattern applies for any future `*.test.tsx` files co-located with routes under `src/routes/__tests__/`.

- **W179 SW4 `resolveRedirectPath` helper + ref-guard useEffect pattern** (2026-05-21). Closes W177 §Honesty #3 state.from race condition. Writer-side at `_auth.tsx:47` uses TanStack canonical `search: { redirect: location.href }`; pre-W179 reader-side at `useLoginFlow.ts:71` used LEGACY React Router pattern `useRouterState({select: s.location.state})` → state.from was always undefined. Fix: 3 callsites (useLoginFlow.ts:71, Login.tsx:48, _public.tsx:46 PublicLayout) read `s.location.search` via useRouterState + parse via shared `frontend/src/utils/redirect.ts:resolveRedirectPath()` helper. Helper accepts absolute URLs (writer's location.href) OR relative paths; same-origin check protects open-redirect; defaults to /dashboard for missing/malformed/cross-origin/non-string input. **CRITICAL `redirectedRef` guard**: navigate({to: target}) clears location.search → useEffect re-fires with undefined → would fall back to /dashboard, OVERRIDING the original /events nav. ref blocks subsequent fires from same component instance. Production: Login.tsx unmounts on navigate; in fast test envs (jsdom + memory history) effect can re-fire on still-mounted instance — ref makes both deterministic. Pattern reusable for any future useEffect that depends on TanStack Router search params + navigates.
- **W179 SW8 `evaluate{Auth,Public,Admin}Guard` pure-function pattern at `frontend/src/routes/guards.ts`** (2026-05-21). Closes W174 §Honesty #4-routeGuards. Pure-function extraction enables unit testing of beforeLoad decision tree. **Critical shape finding via inline probe**: TanStack Router's `redirect()` returns a Response-like object `{options: {to, search, statusCode: 307}}` — assert on `r.options.to` NOT `r.to`. Tests catch the thrown value + assert on `.options.to` + `.options.search?.redirect` (no router runtime needed). `vite.config.mts routeFileIgnorePattern: "__tests__|guards"` REGEX alternation pattern silences TanStack Router generator warning for non-route helpers in `src/routes/`. GuardUser.role optional to accept User.role?: string shape; missing role treated as non-admin in evaluateAdminGuard. Pattern reusable for any future beforeLoad pure-function extraction.
- **W179 SW6 pre-commit gate against raw `docker compose -f docker-compose.full.yml`** (2026-05-21). - **W182 SW4 — chrome-devtools-mcp DOM injection probe for CSS rule verification under LHCI bypass** (2026-05-22). When verifying that a NEW CSS rule renders correctly with its semantic tokens AND the production page state can't trigger that rule (e.g. chat bubble rules need messages; LHCI mock user has 0 messages), inject a test element via `evaluate_script` directly into the rendered DOM scope. Pattern: `themed.appendChild(testDiv)` where `testDiv.innerHTML` has the target className and `getComputedStyle(...)` reads `backgroundImage`/`backgroundColor`/`boxShadow`/`color` returns the resolved token values. Verifies the CSS rule pipeline END-TO-END (rule → token resolution → cascade) without needing backend / mock state injection / Docker chain. Limitation: doesn't verify component-level integration (e.g. ContactList's actual stagger entrance animation needs real contacts data). - **Tailwind v4 `w-full + max-w-N` cross-axis shrink quirk → use `self-stretch + max-w-N + mx-auto` instead** (W182 SW3, 2026-05-22; root cause replacing W181 polish-v1 inline-style workaround). When a parent has `flex flex-col items-center text-center`, the cross-axis is HORIZONTAL. `items-center` resolves `align-items: center` which makes children shrink to **intrinsic content width** unless they explicitly opt out via `align-self`. A child with `w-full max-w-2xl` Tailwind utilities produces `width: 100%; max-width: 42rem;` — and `width: 100%` SHOULD resolve against the parent's cross-axis allocation, but with `align-items: center` the child is positioned as a min-content sized item; the `width: 100%` then resolves against that already-shrunk content box, hence the empirical `offsetWidth: 48px` observed in W181 polish-v1 (verified via chrome-devtools `evaluate_script` showing `computedAlignSelf: "stretch", computedWidth: "48px"`). **Canonical structural fix** (W182 SW3 Agent 2 Option B applied + cross-page audit confirmed no other affected sites in events/feedback/messenger): `<child className="self-stretch text-center max-w-[42rem] mx-auto">` — `self-stretch` explicitly sets `align-self: stretch` so the child fills the cross-axis; `max-w-[42rem]` caps the rendered width; `mx-auto` (margin-inline: auto) ensures the capped element is horizontally centered within the parent's cross-axis allocation. Pattern recipe for future polish work: AVOID `w-full max-w-N` inside `flex-col items-center` parents — always use `self-stretch max-w-N mx-auto` instead. W182 SW3 cross-page audit examined 4 candidates (EventsEmptyState.tsx:24, LoadingState.tsx:28, ProfileModal.tsx:106, NewChatModal.tsx:130+136) — NONE reproduce the `w-full + max-w-N` child pattern (children in those locations use `mx-auto` on already-sized containers, no `w-full` on flex children needing intrinsic width override). Bug is specific to ChatArea empty-state h3 + p structure.

- **MFA test `/users/me → mfa-user` overrides are NOT load-bearing — POST `/auth/login` 202 is the actual MFA trigger** (W177 SW2 Phase 3 finding, 2026-05-21). Pre-W177, MFA tests in Login.test.tsx (transitions to MFA verification + displays errors for invalid OTP attempts) had `server.use(http.get("*/users/me", () => HttpResponse.json({...testUser, mfa_required:true})))` overrides. **These were defensive setup, NOT behaviorally required** for the MFA flow. The actual MFA UI trigger is the POST `/auth/login` 202 response per handlers.ts:655-664 (matches `mfa@example.com + Password123` → returns PendingMfaResponse → useAuthApi.updatePendingMfa → useMfaFlow.loginChallenge becomes truthy → MfaChallengeView renders). W177 SW2 removed these vestigial overrides because they conflicted with the W177 SW1 useEffect (msw LIFO → mfa-user override prepended after renderLogin's 401 override → mfa-user wins → useProfileSync gets mfa-user → setUser populates store → useEffect fires → premature redirect before user can submit credentials). Future MFA-flow tests should NOT add `/users/me` overrides unless they specifically need to verify state-based UI (which would need a different mechanism anyway).

- **CSS percentage heights DON'T resolve against parent's `min-height`** (W183 SW1 FIX-183-01, 2026-05-22). Per CSS spec, child `height: 100%` (Tailwind `h-full`) only resolves when parent has an explicit `height` value — `min-height: 100dvh` (Tailwind `min-h-dvh`) does NOT provide a containing block height; child falls through to `height: auto` and shrinks to content size. Pre-W183 MessengerFeature with `h-full` rendered at 483px / 900px viewport (47% shrinkage) because MainLayout `<main>` had `min-h-dvh` only (Wave 118 SW1 CLS-118-01 footer-anchor protection). **Fix pattern**: parent must set explicit `height` OR `h-[calc(...)]`. For routes that need viewport-fit + retain CLS protection on other routes, gate per-route via `useRouteType.hideFooter`: `className={cn("...", isMessenger ? "h-[calc(100dvh-var(--navbar-h-base,4rem))] overflow-hidden" : "min-h-dvh")}`. Wave 118 CLS protection preserved for non-messenger routes (where footer renders); messenger uses calc to subtract navbar height = exactly viewport. Empirically verified via chrome-devtools-mcp `evaluate_script` reading `offsetHeight` pre-vs-post fix.

- **Blob URL lifecycle pattern for optimistic file uploads** (W183 SW3 + SW7, 2026-05-22). NEVER call `URL.createObjectURL(file)` inline in JSX render — it fires on every re-render + leaks URLs in the browser URL table (no automatic cleanup; references hold the underlying Blob in memory indefinitely). Canonical pattern: **(a)** track URLs in `useRef<Set<string>>` (e.g., `blobUrlsRef.current.add(url)` at creation); **(b)** create ONCE per file at imperative handler (`handleFileSelect` / `handleSendMessage`) — NOT in component body; **(c)** `URL.revokeObjectURL(url)` on mutation success, mutation error, individual file removal, AND component unmount; **(d)** for cleanup-on-unmount use ref-based snapshot via `const blobUrls = blobUrlsRef.current; return () => { blobUrls.forEach(URL.revokeObjectURL) }` — ESLint `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` requires snapshotting `ref.current` to a local variable inside the effect, NOT inside the cleanup function. Applied in `useMessengerController.ts` (optimistic message file attachments) + `MessageInput.tsx` (SmartImage previewUrl per SelectedFile). 18 regression tests in `MessageInput.test.tsx` verify each lifecycle path.

- **useEffect cleanup with setState — React does NOT invoke setState updater during component unmount** (W183 SW11 lesson, 2026-05-22). When useEffect's cleanup function calls `setState(...)`, React batches + drops the update because the component is unmounting. Pattern fails silently — cleanup runs but state is never observably updated. **For cleanup that needs to read latest state at unmount time**, mirror state to a `useRef` updated in a `useEffect([state])` and read from the ref in cleanup. Example: `MessageInput.tsx` uses `selectedFilesRef.current = selectedFiles` + cleanup function reads `selectedFilesRef.current.forEach(f => URL.revokeObjectURL(f.previewUrl))` to revoke Blob URLs at unmount. The ESLint `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` rule sometimes warns on `ref.current` in cleanup; snapshot to local variable inside the effect body first: `const files = selectedFilesRef.current; return () => files.forEach(...)`. Verified by W183 SW11 MessageInput.test.tsx test case "MessageInput unmount fires URL.revokeObjectURL for all tracked Blob URLs" which would have caught the prior setState-in-cleanup pattern silently failing.

- **MessageInput SVG rejection two-layer security pattern** (W183 SW4 + SW11 test coverage, 2026-05-22). User-controlled file uploads can carry XSS payloads via `image/svg+xml` (SVG supports `<script>` tags + inline event handlers). Single-layer MIME check is insufficient — attackers can lie about MIME on upload. Two-layer guard required: **(a)** reject `image/svg+xml` MIME type explicitly; **(b)** reject `.svg` file extension (case-insensitive `endsWith(".svg")` via `name.toLowerCase()`) regardless of declared MIME — file extension is the user-controlled attack vector. For other image MIME types (`image/png`, `image/jpeg`, etc.), additionally sniff the first 512 bytes for `<svg` opening tag (regex with bounded input — annotate with `// eslint-disable-next-line security/detect-unsafe-regex` after manual ReDoS review since pattern is bounded by 512-char window). Pattern recipe for any user-content boundary that accepts file uploads.

- **WebSocket reconnect must have a retry cap — MAX_RECONNECT_ATTEMPTS = 10 with exponential backoff** (W183 SW3, 2026-05-22). Pre-W183 `useChatWebSocket.ts` retried indefinitely on non-clean WS close, generating 2+ `WebSocket connection failed` console errors per retry attempt — under sustained backend outage (dev preview without backend; production network partition) this floods console + browser network panel + DevTools profiling. **Fix pattern**: const `MAX_RECONNECT_ATTEMPTS = 10` + `reconnectAttemptsRef.current` counter that resets on successful connection. Backoff schedule: 1s, 2s, 4s, 8s, 16s, then capped at 30s × 5 = total ~3 min retry window before giving up. After cap, WS stays disconnected; UI surfaces state via banner (W183 SW6 `useMessenger().isConnected` reads from store). Production with backend reachable rarely hits cap; the bug surfaced in dev (LHCI bypass + no backend running). Use `console.warn` → `logError` for the "max retries reached" diagnostic so it's structured for Sentry (W183 SW3 also replaced 2 console.warn callsites).

- **Virtualizer length pass: filter BEFORE useVirtualizer, NOT after** (W184 SW1, 2026-05-23). When wrapping a `@tanstack/react-virtual` list with search/filter UI, the filter MUST be computed BEFORE `useVirtualizer({ count: filteredLength })` and the render iteration MUST consume `filteredArray[virtualRow.index]`, NOT `originalArray[virtualRow.index]`. Using `messages.length` for virtualizer count + `messages[virtualRow.index]` for render with a separate filter applied later causes index misalignment (virtualizer scrolls to indices that don't match the filtered DOM positions; most rows render as nulls). Single source of truth: `filteredMessages = useMemo(...)` → `useVirtualizer({ count: filteredMessages.length })` → `filteredMessages[virtualRow.index]`. Pattern at `frontend/src/components/messenger/ChatWindow.tsx:100-114` (W184 SW1 Path A — ChatArea functional message search).

- **Skeleton row width-jitter via `((idx * N) % M)` math, NOT `Math.random()`** (W184 SW2, 2026-05-23). When rendering N placeholder skeleton rows (e.g., `Array.from({ length: 6 }).map((_, idx) => ...)`), don't use `Math.random()` for per-row width variation (e.g., `width: ${50 + Math.random() * 30}%`) — this causes hydration mismatches in future SSR re-enablement (server-side random ≠ client-side random). Deterministic alternative: `width: ${65 + ((idx * 11) % 25)}%`. Coefficients chosen so the modulo pattern produces visually-varied widths without cycling too quickly. Pattern at `frontend/src/components/messenger/ContactList.tsx:131-140` (W184 SW2 .messenger-skeleton rows) + ChatWindow + NewChatModal.

- **W184 SW3 inline alert decision: keep per-call-site when patterns diverge** (W184 SW3, 2026-05-23). When considering whether to extract a shared component for repeated UI patterns: count the variance across call sites. If ≥3 call sites diverge significantly in (a) mount location, (b) icon choice, (c) button labels, (d) auto-dismiss vs persistent behavior, the shared component's API surface bloats to cover variance without delivering reuse benefit. W184 SW3 considered extracting `<MessengerAlert>` from 4 fetch-failure callsites (ContactList + ChatWindow + NewChatModal) + 1 existing transient alert (MessageInput SVG rejection at :162-172). Patterns diverged on persistent-vs-transient (4 vs 1) + role=alert vs role=status + retry button vs auto-dismiss. **Decision: kept inline per call site**. W185+ refactor possible if 3+ persistent fetch-failure callsites emerge with identical shape. Per `feedback_perfectionism.md` honest framing — defer abstraction until 3+ callsites with identical structure.

- **Lockout test fixture: window seconds + sleep relationship** (W184 SW4, 2026-05-23). `tests/test_auth_lockout.py::test_login_lockout_clears_after_success` (and similar lockout-expiration tests) require **`asyncio.sleep` strictly greater than the configured `auth_lockout_thresholds` window seconds**, NOT just greater than the original timing target. Root cause: `app/services/auth/lockout.py:_calculate_lock_until` uses `attempts[0]` after `_fetch_recent_attempts` reverses DESC SQL result to ASC → `attempts[0] = OLDEST` of top-limit slice → lockout extends `seconds` past that OLDEST attempt (NOT past the most recent attempt despite RZ-W19-03 comment claiming otherwise; implementation-vs-comment disagreement is W185+ backend audit candidate). For test fixtures using `"N:M"` format (N attempts within M seconds), the sleep that "waits for lockout to expire" must be > M to RELIABLY clear the lockout. W184 SW4 widened `"2:1" + sleep 1.2s` → `"2:3" + sleep 3.5s` (sleep 3.5 > window 3, with 0.5s buffer for safety). Sibling `test_login_lockout_race_condition` uses `"2:5"` (no sleep — different assertion flow). General rule: `sleep > seconds + 0.3s buffer` for lockout-expiration tests.

- **framer-motion's `useReducedMotion()` is jsdom-incompatible — use project's `useMediaQuery("(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)")` instead** (W184 SW6, 2026-05-23). framer-motion's `useReducedMotion()` hook calls `window.matchMedia(...).addEventListener(...)` via `initPrefersReducedMotion` (at `node_modules/framer-motion/src/utils/reduced-motion/index.ts:14`) through a code path that **jsdom's default polyfill in `setupTests.ts` doesn't fully cover** — produces `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'addEventListener')` as vitest unhandled error during test runs that mount components using it. Pages mounted in jsdom for tests (Profile.tsx W175 SW4 + Settings.tsx W184 SW6 + others) should use the project's own `useMediaQuery("(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)")` hook from `@/hooks/useMediaQuery` instead — that hook IS jsdom-polyfilled in `setupTests.ts` (W113 SW6 baseline). framer-motion's hook is fine for components/utilities that aren't directly mounted in vitest jsdom tests (e.g., MessengerBackdrop + ProfileBackdrop + SettingsBackdrop run only at app render, not via render() in tests).

- **Profile + Settings polish palette convention** (W184 SW5 + SW6, 2026-05-23). Foundation page polish arcs use distinct color palettes from feature pages to communicate semantic differences. Profile = rose-400 primary + pink-400 accent + amber-300 cozy tertiary (warm/identity-centric — Profile is the user's personal page). Settings = slate-500 primary + purple-400 cool accent + slate-300 lighter tertiary (mostly monochromatic slate for technical/config semantics; purple-400 reserved for active states like tab indicator). Both distinct from 8 prior themed surfaces (Schedule blue, Map teal/cyan, Events amber-500, News sky, Activity emerald, Footer blue-gradient, Admin indigo, Messenger violet/pink/indigo). For Settings specifically: 4 orbs (vs 3 elsewhere) because the 4-tab horizontal layout needs wider visual weight distribution; 4th orb sits at right-edge to balance the wider stage. FIX-77-03 pattern: SettingsBackdrop conditional render is route-level (gated by Settings page rendering), NOT on tab state — tab transitions should NOT cause backdrop to re-mount/flash. Light + dark theme orb opacities bumped 2× in dark per W181 SW6 polish lesson (orbs against near-black slate-950 need ~2× to register vs light bg-page).

- **Auth palette teal/cyan convention** (W186 SW2, 2026-05-23). NEW `frontend/src/styles/tokens/auth.css`: teal-500 PRIMARY + cyan-400 accent + teal-400 sheen. INVERTED from Map's teal-400 PRIMARY for "secure access" semantic distinctness from "navigation" context. primitives.css has only teal-400/500 + cyan-400 available (no teal-300/600), so visual differentiation comes from weight ordering, not new hues. `.auth-card-matte` recipe mirrors `.profile-card-matte` (W184 SW5). `.auth-skeleton` + reduced-motion + print blocks via doubled-class specificity per FIX-72-04. Pattern recipe for any future themed surface in limited-palette primitives constraint.

- **useMediaQuery is DEFAULT export at `@/hooks/useMediaQuery`** (W186 SW3 within-iter sub-fix per W138 Lesson #1, 2026-05-23). `import useMediaQuery from "@/hooks/useMediaQuery"` (NOT `import { useMediaQuery }`). W141 anti-pattern #3 vindication for SAME class as ProfileBackdrop path drift (`features/profile/` vs `components/profile/`). Initial SW3 implementation used named-import — TypeScript errored at gates verification step ("Module has no exported member 'useMediaQuery'. Did you mean to use default import?"). Same lesson applies to ANY future import — verify export style via Read before assuming named vs default.

- **W186 SW1 Path D closure recipe for VITE_LHCI visual verification** (W186 SW1, 2026-05-23). When verifying that an authenticated route renders correctly under VITE_LHCI mock-user (e.g., closing a §Honesty caveat about content visibility): (a) `cd frontend && VITE_LHCI=true npm run build` (W135 SW3 build orchestrator preserves VITE_LHCI=true env); (b) `cd frontend && npx vite preview --port 4173 --strictPort` (background, no Docker chain needed for this verification scope — local vite preview serves the LHCI-build dist directly); (c) Playwright real-Chrome smoke via `node scripts/playwright-visual-smoke.mjs --routes=route1,route2 VISUAL_SMOKE_ORIGIN=http://localhost:4173 VISUAL_SMOKE_OUT_DIR=.screenshots/wave<N>-<purpose>`; (d) manual PNG inspection. PROD build (no VITE_LHCI) verifies UNAUTHENTICATED routes (e.g., /login + /register render with form fields visible) — different verification scope. - **Admin polish W138 Lesson #1 SAME-mechanism bundling pattern** (W186 SW4, 2026-05-23). When multiple micro-fixes across the same feature class can land in 1 SW per W141 anti-pattern #1 STRICT 1-iter, GROUP them. W186 SW4 bundled 5 fixes in 1 commit: (1) useReducedMotion swap framer-motion → useMediaQuery across 2 features (AdminAudit + AdminFeatureFlags) per W184 SW6 jsdom-compat; (2) 6 positional `defaultValue:` antipattern removals in AdminFeatureFlags after Phase 3 Grep verified i18n keys exist in en/admin.json lines 117-134; (3) 2× checkbox focus-visible rings added via replace_all (AdminNotifications); (4) hardcoded `bg-linear-to-r from-blue-500 to-indigo-600` → `bg-(--grad-admin-conic)` admin token (StoriesAdmin token scope violation fix); (5) deferred items (range input touch + AdminNotifications checkbox 44px JSX restructure) to W187+ honestly framed. Recent breaking change in vitest CLI parser. `npx vitest run --silent <file>` errors with `TypeError: Unexpected value "--silent=<file>". Use "--silent=true <file>" instead.` Discovered W187 SW1 verification — first 5× run command failed; corrected within iter as W138 Lesson #1 SAME-mechanism sub-fix.
