- **`describe({ retry: N }, () => {...})` canonical W114/W115 pattern for masking transient timeouts** (W187 SW1, 2026-05-24). Applied at `pageTranslations.test.tsx:560` + `EventsPagination.test.tsx:79` + W187 SW1 `useMessengerController.test.tsx:154` "Blob URL lifecycle". Adds N retries to entire describe block. Masks flake mechanism (does NOT address root cause — e.g., URL mock state-bleed via `Object.defineProperty` is W188+ Path (c) structural refactor candidate via `vi.spyOn`). Use when test failures are non-deterministic + don't require root-cause analysis to unblock CI. W141 anti-pattern #3 92nd vindication: Agent 1 grep for `describe({retry})` returned 0 matches incorrectly; Phase 3 Review caught 2 actual hits empirically.

- **wave165-admin-visual-smoke.mjs `_dark.png` theme fidelity bug** (W187 SW4 PNG inspection discovery, 2026-05-24; PRE-EXISTING since W165 SW3 NOT W187-introduced). Script uses `page.emulateMedia({colorScheme: "dark"})` which does NOT propagate through W127 SW2 cookie-mirror pattern — ThemeProvider reads `ue-mode` cookie + media query fallback only when no cookie set. `_dark.png` captures render LIGHT theme. W164 + W167 §H#4 closures relied on STATIC CSS bundle grep, never visual fidelity. **CLOSED W188 SW2** (3-layer fix: cookie + localStorage via `page.addInitScript` + `page.emulateMedia({colorScheme})` before page.goto). See NEW W188 Gotcha below for full mechanism.

- **Three-layer theme init pattern for headless Chrome SSR-theme parity** (W188 SW2 closure of W187 §H NEW #1, 2026-05-26). Single-layer cookie-only fix (W127 SW2 cookie-mirror) is **insufficient** for Playwright/headless Chrome screenshot capture because client React ThemeContext's `useState(readStoredTheme)` reads localStorage on mount (`frontend/src/contexts/ThemeContext.tsx:18-25`); if empty (fresh Playwright context), defaults to `"system"` → media query → `"light"` in headless Chrome without `--force-colors` flag → client React OVERRIDES the SSR-rendered dark class on hydration. **Canonical fix recipe** (3 layers, all SAME-mechanism "init theme to <theme>" per W138 Lesson #1): (1) `page.context().addCookies([{name:"ue-mode", value:theme, domain, path:"/"}])` — SSR layer; (2) `page.addInitScript((theme) => localStorage.setItem("ue-mode", theme), theme)` — client hydration layer (runs BEFORE any page script per navigation); (3) `page.emulateMedia({colorScheme: theme})` — defense-in-depth for media-query fallback. Apply BEFORE `page.goto` to make all 3 surfaces present when SSR + client hydrate. Pattern recipe in `frontend/scripts/wave165-admin-visual-smoke.mjs:289+` comment block. W141 anti-pattern #3 vindication #97 — single-layer fix DISPROVED on first verification → 3-layer added within same iter.

- **Path D vacuous closure pattern** (W188 SW5 lesson, 2026-05-26). When Agent claims about file state are based on grep heuristics (especially "X surfaces don't have Y" pattern), follow-up direct file Read frequently surfaces false positives. Phase 3 Review catches these before commits. W188 examples: D4 dark-mode parity Agent claimed "6/12 surfaces have NO `.dark` block" — Grep on `.dark .X-theme` across `tokens/` confirmed ALL 11 themed surfaces HAVE `.dark` blocks (Agent error); D1 orphan @property Agent claimed `map.css:22 --map-card-glow + --map-atmosphere-hue` are orphan registrations — direct Read showed lines 20-23 document REMOVAL in W109 + W120 SW6 (Agent misread documentation comment as active code). W141 anti-pattern #3 vindications #94-95. **General rule**: when an audit step is "verify N files for pattern X", ALWAYS use Grep/Glob first then Read affected files; don't trust prose summaries of file state alone.

- **Storybook `stories` glob includes BOTH `src/components/**` AND `src/features/**`** (W193 SW1, 2026-05-28). `.storybook/main.ts:15` carries two explicit glob patterns so feature-co-located stories (under `src/features/`) are discoverable — the codebase migrated features into `src/features/` over ~80 waves (Activity W112, Events/News, Admin W164, Messenger W145) but the glob was frozen at `src/components/**` since W115, silently orphaning every `features/`-co-located story (6 events/news stories were dormant). Neither pattern matches `src/routes/`, so `routes/_admin/admin.stories.tsx` (a TanStack Router route file, NOT a story) stays excluded BY CONSTRUCTION — no negation needed. NEW stories under `src/features/<x>/` are now picked up; NEW stories under `src/routes/` are NOT (by design). **Backdrop story decorators**: scope-defined-theme-token backdrops (activity/admin/auth/profile/settings/events/news/map — orb tokens defined under `.X-theme`, NOT `@property`-registered globals like messenger's) need a `themed(dark)` decorator factory that nests `.dark` OUTSIDE the `.X-theme` class. `.dark .X-theme` is a DESCENDANT selector + Storybook nests story decorators INSIDE meta decorators, so a "meta=theme + story=.dark" split (the MessengerBackdrop template) inverts the order → silently renders light orbs in the "DarkMode" variant. FooterBackdrop is the exception (theme-agnostic always-dark, no `.X-theme`; decorator wraps in `bg-footer` + `--text-on-footer` white label). The factory's returned arrow trips `react/display-name` — use a block-body factory + justified `eslint-disable-next-line` (W112 SW1 pattern; Storybook decorators aren't render components).

- **Rolldown chunk filename-hash ≠ content sha256** (W193 SW5, 2026-05-28). A clean prod build can shift `dist/client/assets/index-<hash>.js` filename (e.g. W190 `CGBUMlAV` → W193 `B8BD2TjY`) while `sha256sum` proves the emitted bytes are BYTE-IDENTICAL — Rolldown's filename-hash folds in module-graph metadata that unbundled file additions (new `.stories.tsx`) perturb without changing chunk content. **Verify the bundle invariant via content `sha256sum`, NOT the filename.** Same class as the server.js sha drift tracked since W189 (adding `.stories.tsx` shifts server.js sha while size + behavior unchanged). Corollary lint gotcha: committing a `.storybook/*.ts` file makes lint-staged's `eslint --fix` emit a non-blocking `Parsing error: ... not found by the project service` (`.storybook/` is outside eslint's typed-lint tsconfig); harmless + pre-existing (W123/W125 hit it); CI unaffected (`npm run lint` scopes `src`+`tests`). CLOSED W193 polish-v1: `.storybook` added to eslint `ignores` (mirrors the pre-existing `vite.config.mts` entry) + `--no-warn-ignored` on the lint-staged eslint task → `.storybook/*.ts` commits are now fully silent (exit 0).

- **MapLibre markers in Storybook need a minimal `<Map>` decorator + empty offline mapStyle** (W194 SW4, 2026-05-28). `react-map-gl/maplibre` `<Marker>` components (BuildingMarker/POIMarker/EventMarker) throw without a `<Map>` ancestor. Wrap each marker story in `<Map initialViewState={{longitude, latitude, zoom}} mapStyle={EMPTY_STYLE} attributionControl={false} style={{ width: "100%", height: "100%" }}>` inside a fixed-size container, where `const EMPTY_STYLE: StyleSpecification = { version: 8, sources: {}, layers: [] }` (typed from `maplibre-gl`) — the empty offline style avoids ALL network tile fetches (markers are HTML overlays positioned once maplibre inits, independent of basemap paint). Import `maplibre-gl/dist/maplibre-gl.css`. Coord gotcha FIX-100-01: data is `geoCoords [lat,lng]` → `longitude={coords[1]} latitude={coords[0]}` (never swap). **Verified rendering in the real-Chromium Storybook iframe** via real-Chrome Playwright spike (maplibre WebGL inits + pin visible + 0 console errors, incl EventMarker popup's TanStack `<Link to="/events/$id">` against the preview memory-router) — Wave 147 SW5's HEADLESS canvas-never-visible issue does NOT apply. `@storybook/addon-vitest` does NOT run these stories in jsdom (vitest count unchanged), so no WebGL-in-jsdom failure.
- **Storybook story-worthiness ≠ "few props" — the axis is "renders meaningful UI from args alone"** (W195, 2026-05-29). Several `[LEAF]`-tagged components are NOT clean static-story candidates: *hooks* misfiled as components (`EventFilterPopover` exports a hook `useEventFilterPopover`, not a component), *stateful-no-props* components that render `null` until a browser/keyboard event (`OfflineIndicator`/`SyncStatus` online-event-driven; `EventsShortcutsOverlay`/`NewsShortcutsOverlay` `?`-keypress toggle), and *portal-to-body* dialogs whose dark mode escapes the decorator's `.dark` scope (`Dialog`/`EventQrDialog` portal to `document.body`). Substitute, don't fight (per-SW rule, W138 L#1). When a component needs an i18n `t`/`TFunction` prop (NavbarLogo/MobileDrawer\*), supply it via a tiny harness that calls the real `useTranslation()` inside the preview `I18nextProvider` rather than casting a fake `TFunction`. **And `IntersectionObserver` `rootMargin` accepts px/% ONLY, never `rem`** — native browsers throw `SyntaxError: rootMargin must be specified in pixels or percent`; jsdom IO mocks are lenient (unit tests miss it) + an unused-in-prod component hides it (tree-shaken) → a real-browser Storybook render is the gate that catches it (W195 SW6-fix: AsyncImage `12.5rem` → `200px`, zero prod-bundle delta).
- **Storybook overlay story-worthiness: controlled (`open` prop) = LEAF; self-toggle (no prop) = SKIP** (W196, 2026-05-29). MapShortcutsOverlay takes `open`/`onClose` (a story passing `open: true` renders the dialog → clean LEAF), whereas EventsShortcutsOverlay/NewsShortcutsOverlay are zero-prop, own their `open` via `useState`+`window keydown` (`?`-toggle) and `if(!open) return null` → a static story renders nothing → SKIP (Phase 3 read corrected Agent 1, matching the W195 audit). Two more W196-confirmed Storybook patterns: (a) a TanStack **`<Link to="/typed/$id">` renders its anchor in Storybook's root-only preview router WITHOUT throwing** (proven by W195 NewsDetailNavigation + W196 EventCardContent/NewsCardContent) — so "CONTEXT" cards that only use `<Link>`/`useTranslation`/`useAuth`/`useQuery` are storyable via the global decorators alone (`preview.tsx` already provides RouterProvider + AuthContext(admin) + QueryClientProvider + I18nextProvider; the providers they "need" are ambient); (b) for TanStack-table sub-components (`DataTableColumnHeader`/`DataTablePagination`), build a real `useReactTable({ data, columns, ...rowModels })` harness mirroring `DataTable.tsx` to supply the `column`/`table` prop. And a component that calls a data hook internally with NO prop seam + `if(!data) return null` (MapWeatherBadge → `useMapWeather()`) renders nothing statically → SKIP/defer even though it "has few props" — pass its data DOWN to a controlled child instead (MapWeatherBadge → MapWeatherPanel, which IS a clean controlled-props LEAF).
- **Storybook CONTEXT-tier provider-harness selection by export surface** (W197, 2026-05-29). Pick the *real* provider when it's exported + side-effect-free (`SchedulePageProvider` for Schedule tables/dialogs; `AppShellProvider` for MapSidebar — `useAppShell()` throws without it); stub the (newly-exported) context when the real provider does impure work (`MessengerContext.Provider` value-stub for ChatArea, since `MessengerProvider` runs WebSocket+query — W197 SW7 added `export const MessengerContext`, additive/unused-by-app/tree-shaken byte-identical, verified Build × 3). Portal components (`@/components/ui/Dialog` + `@/components/settings/ui/Dialogs` via `createPortal` to `document.body`) escape themed decorators → default-theme-only stories (EventQrDialog pattern: no `themed` wrapper, `layout: "fullscreen"`, no DarkMode variant). Schedule dialogs open via a mount-effect `OpenDialogHarness` calling `useSchedulePage().openDialog(type[, lesson])` inside `<SchedulePageProvider>` (each dialog gates on `activeDialog === type`). `MapControls` reads its map only in imperative handlers → `useRef<MapRef|null>(null)` renders the full panel with no live `<Map>`. `useSpotlight()` is an exported hook → CardViews (NewsCardView/EventCardView) story via an `Omit<…Props,"spotlight">` harness calling it (no MotionValue mock). `RelatedNews`/`RelatedEvents` take `items[]` directly (no internal `useQuery`) → cheap prop-driven, no query-seeding decorator needed. **Generated `*Out` fixtures carry required readonly `*_optimized` fields** (`image_url_optimized` on NewsOut+EventOut; `avatar_url_optimized`+`cover_url_optimized` on UserOut) — a `[a-z_]+:`-filtered grep hides them; include them or tsc fails (W138 L#1 within-SW fix bit both SW2 + SW3).
- **The 3 messenger/events/news "logic-wrapper" cards degrade gracefully — no module-mocking needed for Storybook** (W198, 2026-05-29). The opening-prompt assumption that EventCard / NewsCard / NewChatModal are "gated on module-mocking" was OVERTURNED by direct component reads (W141 #3): **EventCard** (`components/events/EventCard/EventCard.tsx`) makes **zero network on mount** — `useEventRegistration.sync()`'s only `api.get` is click-only inside `try/catch { return null }`; mount effects touch only guarded localStorage; it's fully props-driven (`Partial<Event>`) and delegates to the already-storied `EventCardView`. **NewsCard** passes `initialData` into `useNewsInteraction`, so prop values render immediately and a failed background refetch is silent under `retry:false` (IndexedDB/localStorage/BroadcastChannel all work in real-browser Storybook). **NewChatModal**'s `/users` `useQuery` is `enabled: open && debouncedSearch.length > 1` — idle until the user types, so the base `{open:true}` story = zero network; rich variants seed via per-story `queryClient.setQueryData(["users", "<term>"], usersFixture)`. **Do NOT build MSW-in-Storybook** for these — it's the exact Storybook + Vite 8/Rolldown service-worker fragility class behind the W120-W123 Chromatic saga; the prop-fixture (+ light `setQueryData`) kit covers them with zero `.storybook` change (bundle stays byte-identical). Generally: before assuming a card "needs mocking," read it — graceful degradation (zero-mount-fetch / `initialData` / `enabled`-gating) is the common case in this codebase. (Also: `useNotifications`'s fire-and-forget `checkSchedule()` resolves cleanly because the generated API client RETURNS errors and only throws on per-call `throwOnError` — so NotificationsBell/UserMenu stories don't unhandled-reject.)
- **`.stories.tsx` files MUST be excluded from vitest coverage** (W198 polish, 2026-05-29). `frontend/vitest.config.ts` `coverage.exclude` now carries `"src/**/*.stories.{ts,tsx}"`. CI runs `npm run test:ci` = `vitest run --coverage` with a **global 70% lines/statements/functions threshold** (`thresholds` block). The story-coverage campaign added 184 `.stories.tsx` files — most under `src/components/**` (already excluded by `"src/components/**/*"`), but **stories under `src/features/**`** (e.g. `features/activity/components/*.stories.tsx`) were NOT excluded, so v8's `all: true` counted them as 0%-covered files and **diluted global coverage below 70%** (W198 tipped lines 70.0 → 69.48, breaking CI even though all 1270 tests passed). Stories are Storybook/Chromatic artifacts — tree-shaken out of the app bundle (byte-identical sha proves it), never executed by the test runner, never production code paths → counting them in coverage is a **measurement bug**, not a quality gap. The `src/**/*.stories.{ts,tsx}` glob is the principled, directory-agnostic fix (vs over-excluding all of `src/features/**`, which would drop real feature-code from the coverage denominator). **Local trap:** plain `vitest run` (no `--coverage`) does NOT surface this — always run `npm run test:ci` locally before claiming a story wave is CI-clean. **Arithmetic note:** excluding 0%-covered files can only *raise* the remaining set's coverage % (numerator unchanged, denominator shrinks); local 69.93% functions readings under heavy setup-churn are an under-execution artifact, not the CI value.
- **React Compiler is a build-gate sharper than tsc/eslint** (W199, 2026-05-29). The `react-compiler/react-compiler` ESLint rule can be `eslint-disable`'d, but the **React Compiler Babel transform** (`@rolldown/plugin-babel`, run at `npm run build` / `build-storybook`) does its OWN analysis and **throws `ReactCompilerError`** on a render-phase `use*`-namespace reference (e.g. `useAuthStore.setState(...)` called in a component's render body) — independent of the lint directive. So this class **only surfaces at build-storybook / build, never at the per-SW tsc + eslint gate** (W199 SW6 `SpotifyConnect.stories.tsx` shipped tsc + eslint-clean with an `eslint-disable-next-line react-compiler/react-compiler`, then FAILED `build-storybook` with `ReactCompilerError: Hooks may not be referenced as normal values`). Robust fix: never reference the `use*`-namespace value in render — seed external (Zustand) stores inside `useEffect` (the cleanup-only `setState` empirically did NOT trip the rule → render-phase-specific). Extends the W128 SW1 `readSsrAuthHint` `use*`-namespace false-positive class.
- **Storying a scroll-gated component** (W200, 2026-05-29). A component gated on `window.scrollY > N` via a `scroll` event listener IS storyable in Storybook: in a decorator's `useEffect`, redefine `window.scrollY` (`Object.defineProperty(window, "scrollY", { value, configurable: true, writable: true })`) + dispatch a synthetic `scroll` Event **deferred via `requestAnimationFrame`** (so the component's own mount-effect listener attaches first; restore `scrollY = 0` on cleanup) → the value-readable gate flips deterministically. BUT a SIBLING `IntersectionObserver` gate (LAYOUT-driven, e.g. BackToTop's footer-offset at `BackToTop.tsx:26-47` lifting the FAB above `[role=contentinfo]`) is NOT value-mockable — faking `scrollY` does not fire it, and real scroll is Chromatic-flaky → render a static `[role=contentinfo]` target below the fold (`top: 140vh`) to exercise ONLY the observer's attach branch (it null-guards otherwise) and treat the layout-driven repositioning as a deliberate non-goal. Chromium-only: redefining `scrollY` requires `configurable: true` (Chromatic + the real-Chrome runtime smoke are both Chromium). Pattern: `BackToTop.stories.tsx` `ScrollGate` harness (named to avoid shadowing the real `ScrollReveal` component in `motion/`).
- **Chromatic enforce-readiness** (W201, 2026-05-30). A story is snapshot-deterministic only if its rendered pixels are identical between two CI runs of the SAME code. `parameters.chromatic.pauseAnimationAtEnd: true` achieves that for framer-motion springs (Chromatic waits for the settled final frame), but NOT for three classes that need `parameters.chromatic.disableSnapshot: true`: (1) **canvas `Math.random()` swarms** — no final frame (WeatherParticles, ParticleAuthBackground, MfaChallengeView's particle bg); (2) **WebGL + remote tiles** — GPU raster + network both vary run-to-run (MapLibreMap); (3) **live wall-clock text** — countdowns / `Date.now()`-relative `timeStatus` / relative-time strings recompute against real `now`, drifting day-over-day (FlipCountdown, EventCard). Mark these BEFORE the first baseline, else a baseline polluted with perpetually-red stories trains the team to ignore Chromatic. `disableSnapshot` keeps the story in the Storybook index (dev/docs intact) — it only skips the Chromatic snapshot. `chromatic.yml` is gated `if: vars.CHROMATIC_ENABLED == 'true'` (skips cleanly until the token Secret + flag are set) and runs Report-mode (`exitZeroOnChanges: true`) until a deliberate enforce-flip to `false`. Project-token (`chpt_…`) lives ONLY in the `CHROMATIC_PROJECT_TOKEN` Secret + `memory/wave122_chromatic_upstream.md` — never hardcoded in the workflow (W201 hygiene).
- **`--messenger-attachment-bg` is a white-veil token, NOT a theme-inverted token** (W202 SW3, 2026-05-30). The file-attachment chip in `ChatWindow.tsx` renders inside BOTH the violet SENT bubble (theme-independent gradient) and the theme-neutral RECEIVED bubble — so it has no single correct background across the 4 sent/received × light/dark states. Fix: NEW `--messenger-attachment-bg` (+`-hover`) in `tokens/messenger.css` `.messenger-theme` = a low-opacity **white veil** (`color-mix(in srgb, white 14%, transparent)`) with **NO `.dark` override** (it sits over the violet sent bubble, which is the same hue in both themes). The chip is 4-state-correct only when SENT uses the veil token while RECEIVED uses `--bg-surface-raised` (the white veil vanishes on a light received bubble) — do NOT unify both branches onto one token. The real dark-contrast bug was the SHARED file-icon container: make its glyph conditional (`text-[var(--text-inverse)]` on sent / `text-(--brand-main)` on received), not a single hardcoded color. Same class as the W116 SW3 `bg-brand text-[var(--text-inverse)]` theme-token discipline, but for an element layered over a theme-independent surface.
- **`.messenger-online-pulse` is wired to the active-chat header avatar ONLY** (W202 SW5, 2026-05-30). The pulsing-presence keyframe (`tokens/messenger.css:555-582`, reduced-motion-guarded at 683-686) was an orphan until W202. It runs ONE infinite animation, so it belongs only where the conversation is open (the `ChatArea.tsx` header avatar). ContactList rows + ProfileModal keep the STATIC `.messenger-online-indicator` dot — never pulse N list rows (perf + visual-noise). When adding presence cues elsewhere, default to the static indicator; reserve the pulse for singular, in-focus contexts.
- **WS `validated.message` is a Valibot `ParsedMessage`, NOT `@/api/chat` `Message`** (W202 SW2, 2026-05-30). In `useChatWebSocket.ts` the `case "new_message"` payload comes from `parseWsMessage` (`api/schemas/wsMessage.ts`) where `attachments`/`sender` are `Record<string,unknown>` — structurally NOT the app `Message` (`Attachment[]`/`User`). So a bare `validated.message` is NOT assignable to `Message` and the cast cannot be deleted (tsc fails). The correct shape is a SINGLE `as Message` (the app `Message` IS assignable to `ParsedMessage`, so the widening is sound for cache insertion). Keep the explanatory comment — it stops a future "redundant cast, delete it" cleanup from breaking the build, and records that WS frames are already schema-validated by `parseWsMessage` (security-relevant). An audit flagging this as a "redundant double-cast" is a verify-before-write hazard (W141 #3).
- **ChatWindow animate-only-NEW-messages boundary pattern** (W202 SW6b, 2026-05-30). A `@tanstack/react-virtual` message list re-runs each bubble's mount `initial` animation every time the row scrolls back into view (disorienting + perf anti-pattern). Fix without ref-reads-in-render (React Compiler safe): `const [animateFromIndex, setAnimateFromIndex] = useState(Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY)`; bump it to `filteredMessages.length` INSIDE the existing auto-scroll `useEffect`'s if-block; then `const animateEntrance = !prefersReducedMotion && !isSearchActive && virtualRow.index >= animateFromIndex` drives `initial={animateEntrance ? {opacity:0,y:10,scale:0.95} : false}`. The `POSITIVE_INFINITY` initial value is load-bearing — it treats every message present at first paint as already-seen (no entrance), because the state initializer runs BEFORE the isLoading early-returns (a lazy-init reading `filteredMessages.length` would stampede). State is read in render, ref only in effects → passes `react-compiler/react-compiler` eslint AND the `@rolldown/plugin-babel` build-gate (verify both; the Babel transform is a stricter gate than eslint per the W199 SpotifyConnect Gotcha). **The boundary is per-component-instance state, so the host MUST be keyed by chat identity** — `key={selectedChatId}` on `<ChatWindow>` in `ChatArea.tsx` (W202 polish-v1). On desktop `showChat` is always true so `ChatWindow` is a *persistent* instance with no remount on contact switch; without the key it carries the previous chat's boundary into the next chat and animates its existing tail on switch. The key also resets the virtualizer + auto-scroll so a switched-to chat starts at the bottom. Same lesson class for any per-instance-state animation gate inside a persistent two-pane layout: key it by the entity identity.
- **Schema-added fields do NOT retrofit hand-written `MessageResponse` constructors** (W203 SW8, 2026-05-30). `app/services/chat/query_service.py` builds `MessageResponse(...)` field-by-field in `get_messages` (line ~203) and the `get_chats` last-message builder (line ~110) — an explicit projection that deliberately omits the full `sender` to avoid N+1. Adding `read_at` to the Pydantic schema (SW3) carried it through `from_attributes`/`model_dump()` paths (the WS serializer + command_service) but the explicit REST projections silently defaulted it to `= None` → `GET /messages` returned `read_at:null` despite the DB row having a timestamp, and the live read-receipt marker never rendered on refetch. **When adding a `Message` field, audit EVERY explicit `MessageResponse(...)` construction site, not just the schema.** Pinned by `test_get_messages_surfaces_read_at`.
- **A `useMutation`-object dependency in a `useCallback` consumed by an unconditional effect is an infinite re-fire loop** (W203 SW8, 2026-05-30). React Query v5 returns a NEW mutation result object on every status transition (idle→pending→success). `markAsRead = useCallback(c => mut.mutate(c), [mut])` consumed by `useEffect(() => mark(id), [id, markAsRead])` re-fires forever: mutate → status change → new `mut` object → new `markAsRead` → effect's dep changed → re-fires → mutate… In `useMessengerController` this fired **hundreds** of `POST /chats/{id}/read`, capped only by the 429 rate-limiter (pre-existing; read receipts made mark-read load-bearing enough to surface it). **Fix: depend on the referentially-stable `.mutate`** (`const m = mut.mutate; useCallback(c => m(c), [m])`) — React Query guarantees `.mutate` stable for the mutation lifetime, and React Compiler re-derives memoization from the captured stable value (`Object.is`). **Verify mark-read-style effects with a live network trace, not just unit tests** — single-render asserts never observe the status→re-render→re-fire cycle.
- **Chat-level ephemeral read frame** (W203 SW4, 2026-05-30). Read receipts broadcast `{type:"read", chat_id, user_id (the READER), read_at}` via inline `ws_manager.broadcast_to_chat(..., exclude_user_id=reader)` (the ephemeral tier — typing/presence/read), NOT the durable domain-event/outbox tier (reserved for `new_message`). `mark_messages_read` generates `read_at = utc_now()` in Python (no SQL `func.now()` round-trip), returns `(read_at, affected)`; the service/dispatcher broadcast AFTER commit (read-your-write) + ONLY when `affected > 0` (repeated chat opens with 0 new unread → no churn). The FE cache-flip predicate is `sender_id !== reader_id` (in 1-on-1 that's exactly "my sent messages"). **Caveat**: the LIVE push needs the ws-hub↔backend broadcast bridge (absent in dev, same as `new_message`); the feature self-heals via the persisted `read_at` on the next `getMessages`.
- **`WeakValueDictionary` single-flight cache needs a LOCAL strong ref** (W203 SW8, 2026-05-30). `connection_manager._get_chat_participants_cached` keeps per-chat single-flight locks in a `WeakValueDictionary[uuid.UUID, asyncio.Lock]`. The pattern `if k not in d: d[k] = asyncio.Lock()` then `lock = d[k]` **deterministically KeyErrors**: `d[k] = asyncio.Lock()` stores only a *weak* reference to a temporary that has no strong reference, so CPython refcounting reclaims it at end-of-statement → the read-back `d[k]` finds a dead weakref. (The pre-existing RZ-14-04 "two-step" comment wrongly believed this was safe.) Correct pattern binds the local strong ref FIRST: `lock = d.get(k); if lock is None: lock = asyncio.Lock(); d[k] = lock` — the local `lock` keeps the object alive across the `async with lock:` block. Surfaced by W203 SW4's REST `mark_read` broadcast (the first end-to-end caller of `broadcast_to_chat` in the test suite through this branch with the cache disabled) — `tests/test_chat_api.py::test_mark_read_logic` `KeyError(UUID)`, caught by CI's full backend suite (2904 tests), NOT the 3 chat slices run locally. **Lesson: a change that adds the first end-to-end caller of a shared hot path can surface a latent bug — run the FULL backend `pytest`, not a slice, before declaring a wave CI-clean.**

- **The live messenger WS bridge chain is DEV-only** (W204, 2026-05-30). browser↔**ws-hub (Go)** (`/ws/chat` → Caddy → ws-hub `/ws`, W173) vs the backend's in-process Python `ws_manager` — these are two separate fan-out paths. W204 bridges them: `broadcast_to_chat` ([app/api/ws/connection_manager.py](app/api/ws/connection_manager.py)) → `broker.publish_core(f"chat.{chat_id}", {type, room, payload})` (core NATS) → ws-hub's existing `chat.*` core subscription → per-connection room fan-out → browser. **Only `docker-compose.full.yml` (dev) runs ws-hub + nats; the prod compose + k8s have NO ws-hub** → the live bridge is DEV-only until a prod ws-hub deploy infra wave; prod still self-heals via refetch. Read receipts go live **synchronously** (`mark_read` → `broadcast_to_chat` directly); new_message is **async** (outbox producer — see below).
- **`publish_core` MUST use orjson + publish-only-if-connected** (W204 SW1, 2026-05-30). `serialize_message` ([app/api/ws/serializers.py](app/api/ws/serializers.py)) returns raw `uuid.UUID` for id/chat_id/sender_id → stdlib `json.dumps` crashes (`TypeError: UUID not serializable`); use `orjson.dumps(payload, default=str)` (native UUID+datetime). **NEVER connect from this ephemeral hot path** (`if self._nc is None or not self._nc.is_connected: return`) — connecting would add a multi-second timeout to message-send during a NATS outage + raise in test/CLI; the broker's background reconnect restores `_nc`, frames self-heal via refetch.
- **ws-hub room-join authz path is `/api/v1/chat/check-participant`** (W204 SW7, 2026-05-30; W173 dormant-routing-gap class). `services/ws-hub/pkg/hub/auth_client.go`'s `CanJoinRoom` calls the backend's internal chat router, which mounts under `API_V1_PREFIX` ("/api/v1") in `app/api/internal/__init__.py` — NOT `/api/internal/...`. The old hardcoded `/api/internal/chat/check-participant` 404'd → fail-closed room-join → no live `chat.{id}` fan-out reached the browser. Dormant because no client sent a "join" until W204 wired the frontend join (same class as the W173 `/ws` routing fixes — surfaced only when /messenger is exercised end-to-end). Empirically `/api/v1/...`→200 vs `/api/internal/...`→404.
- **NATS→ws-hub→room fan-out can't do per-recipient exclusion** → the frontend self-echo guard is load-bearing (W204 SW4, 2026-05-30). The in-process path excludes the sender (`exclude_user_id`), but the NATS mirror delivers to ALL room members including the sender's own browser. `useChatWebSocket.ts` skips `new_message` if `message.sender_id === currentUserId` + `read` if `user_id === currentUserId` (`currentUserId` threaded via MessengerContext from `useAuth`). It's **user-level**, so a 2nd tab of the same user won't live-show that user's own sends (self-heals on refetch). ws-hub room membership is **per-connection** → `ws.onopen` must rejoin the active room (`activeRoomRef`). `parseWsMessage` unwraps the ws-hub `{type, room, payload}` envelope keyed on **payload-presence** (not outer type) so ws-hub's notification re-typing is robust.
- **new_message live in dev depends on the async outbox producer** (W204 (z)#2, 2026-05-30; W205+ investigation). `mark_read` → `broadcast_to_chat` is synchronous (live now via the bridge), but `new_message` broadcasts only via `send_message` → `MessageSent` → `capture_domain_events` after_flush → reactive `OutboxWorker` (LISTEN `outbox_events`) → `handle_message_sent` → `notify_new_message` → `broadcast_to_chat`. In the W204 dev session this chain didn't complete (`stored_events` + `failed_outbox_events` both empty after sends + no post-rebuild OutboxWorker processing; a 14s userB-foreground poll caught nothing → not a timing artifact). Upstream of + independent of the W204 bridge. When verifying new_message live, first confirm the `MessageSent` StoredEvent is written + the reactive OutboxWorker processes it in the dev container. **W204 polish-v1 SHARPENED the root cause**: the OutboxWorker IS running (Reactive Mode, listening) + `register_event_listeners()` IS called (lifespan.py:405, both `after_flush` + `after_flush_postexec` registered + logged) + `send_message` DOES call `record_event(MessageSent)` unconditionally (command_service.py:303, ARCH-BE-01) — **yet `stored_events` is EMPTY for ALL aggregate types over the backend's uptime** (user.created/event.created/chat.message_sent all absent), `failed_outbox_events` empty, worker never logged a processed event. So the entire dev domain-event capture pipeline produces ZERO StoredEvents — a **systemic, pre-existing dev-environment issue** affecting every event-driven feature (notifications/embeddings/chat), not a W204 defect. Read receipts are unaffected because `mark_read` broadcasts synchronously (bypasses the outbox) — why W203 never surfaced it. The synchronous `notify_new_message` in `send_message` is commented out (command_service.py:377), so new_message has NO non-outbox fallback. W205+ start point.

- **The outbox `handle_message_sent` handler MUST fetch the sender by id, NOT use `message.sender`** (W205 SW9, 2026-05-31; closes the W204 (z)#2 new_message-live gap once the capture fires). `handle_message_sent` ([app/services/event_handlers.py](app/services/event_handlers.py)) does `message = await db.get(models.Message, event.message_id)`, and `Message.sender` is `lazy="noload"` (the CLAUDE.md N+1 guard) → `message.sender` is **None**. Passing it to `notify_new_message(sender=...)` crashed on `exclude_user_id=sender.id` (`AttributeError: 'NoneType' has no attribute 'id'`) → the new_message broadcast never fired. Fix: `sender = await db.get(models.User, message.sender_id)` + None-guard, then `message.sender = sender` (in-memory reassignment, same session — no extra query/flush) so `serialize_message` enriches the frame. **The bug was dormant for waves** because the outbox produced zero events (W204 (z)#2); the W205 SW-A `capture_on_commit` fix ran the chain end-to-end for the first time and exposed it. The outbox handler was previously UNTESTED — add a `db.get`-mock regression test for any new outbox handler.
- **`MessageResponse.content` must allow `""` for the D1 soft-delete tombstone** (W205 SW9, 2026-05-31). `MessageBase.content` is `Field(..., min_length=1, max_length=2000)` (shared with `MessageCreate` input). `MessageResponse` inherits it, but a soft-deleted message clears `content=""` (D1) → `query_service.get_messages` (which builds `MessageResponse` field-by-field) 500'd with pydantic `string_too_short` the moment a chat held a deleted message. Fix: override `content: str = Field(..., max_length=2000)` in `MessageResponse` ([app/schemas/chat.py](app/schemas/chat.py)) — keeps content REQUIRED (only the min floor drops); `MessageCreate` + the POST/PATCH `Form(..., min_length=1)` keep INPUT strict. Test the real pydantic model (not a SimpleNamespace stand-in — the SW4 serialize tests missed this).
- **Valibot `v.optional(X)` accepts `undefined` but REJECTS `null`** (W205 SW9, 2026-05-31). A backend field that serializes as `null` (not omitted) — e.g. `serialize_message` emits `"sender": null` when `Message.sender` is noload — must be `v.optional(v.nullable(X))` in the frontend schema, NOT `v.optional(X)`. Pre-fix, `MessageSchema.sender` was `v.optional(v.record(...))` → a new_message frame with `"sender": null` failed `parseWsMessage` → the WHOLE frame was dropped (`[ws] Invalid frame dropped`) → new_message never rendered live. The `read_at` field already had the correct `v.optional(v.nullable(v.string()))` pattern; mirror it for any nullable backend field (`wsMessage.ts` `MessageSchema`).
- **A central domain-event/serializer fix surfaces a cascade of dormant downstream bugs** (W205 meta-pattern, extends W203 §H#5). The SW-A `capture_on_commit` fix restored the domain-event subsystem and thereby ran the producer→broadcast→browser chain end-to-end for the first time in many waves — exposing 4 latent bugs (noload-sender crash + content-min_length 500 + sender:null Valibot drop + a stale test stand-in) that had sat dormant while the chain never completed. When a wave restores a long-broken subsystem: (a) run the FULL backend pytest (W203 §H#5 — a slice misses sibling-file breakage), and (b) verify the feature LIVE end-to-end (each downstream layer that never ran is a latent-bug candidate). Each was a within-iter bounded ≤1-fix follow-up (W138 L#1), not a mechanism pivot.
- **OpenAPI contract snapshot regen: write LF + superset allows ADDITIONS but not REMOVALS** (W205 SW9, 2026-05-31). `tests/contracts/test_openapi_contract.py` is a SUPERSET check (`assert_openapi_superset` — snapshot keys ⊆ current), so ADDING fields/routes is safe (W122 note) but REMOVING a key (e.g. relaxing `content` min_length) breaks it → regenerate `tests/contracts/snapshots/api_openapi_v1.json` via `json.dumps(normalize_openapi(load_current_openapi()), indent=2, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False)`. On Windows, `open('w')` text-mode writes CRLF → a regular `diff` against the LF snapshot shows a false ~2× (24K-line) diff; use `newline='\n'` (or `diff --strip-trailing-cr`) to see the real W205-scoped diff.

- **Reaction emoji selector is a QUERY param, not a URL-path segment** (W206 SW7, 2026-05-31). `DELETE /chats/{c}/messages/{m}/reactions?emoji=` — query params decode unambiguously (`parse_qs`); arbitrary multi-codepoint content in a URL path segment is a known fragility class, so it's avoided. **Honest re-attribution (W141 #4)**: the mid-wave path→query switch was FIRST blamed on a Caddy path mis-decode, but live verification overturned that — the earlier "failed remove" was a CORRUPT stored value (next entry), not a route bug. The query-param route is PROVEN live two-browser (real 👍 add + remove cross-user); the path-segment route was never verified for a real emoji.
- **curl on Windows Git-Bash mangles a literal multi-byte emoji in a request BODY to `??` (`3f3f`)** (W206 SW7 (z)#1, 2026-05-31). A curl `POST FormData emoji=👍` stored `??` (2 ASCII chars, hex `3f3f`), so no remove (path OR query) could ever match the correctly-encoded 👍. Root-caused via a DB byte-check `encode(emoji::bytea,'hex')` (browser-added 😢=`f09f98a2`; curl-added 👍=`3f3f`). URL percent-escapes (`%F0%9F%91%8D`) are pure ASCII → curl transmits them fine; only the literal-emoji-in-body is mangled. **Live emoji ADD verification must use the BROWSER** (correct UTF-8), NOT curl; curl is fine for percent-encoded URL/query values.
- **Reaction delta-frame: self-echo guard + drift-self-heals + per-viewer `reacted_by_me`** (W206 SW3/SW5, 2026-05-31). The `reaction_changed` broadcast carries the actor's `user_id` + a `{action: "added"|"removed"}` delta (the W203 read-frame archetype). The FE self-echo-guards the actor (`validated.user_id === currentUserIdRef.current` — already patched optimistically); other clients patch count ±1 via `applyReactionChangedFrame`. `reacted_by_me` is **per-viewer** → server-computed on REST (`_aggregate_reactions`), client-derived elsewhere, **never** in a broadcast frame. The non-idempotent delta drifts but self-heals on the next `GET /messages` (accepted, same as read/new_message).
- **Reaction repo idempotency + `selectinload` aggregation + the W203-SW8 two-site rule** (W206 SW2/SW3, 2026-05-31). `message_reactions` is a separate CHILD table (mirrors `Attachment` — `UUID7PrimaryKeyMixin`, `lazy=noload`, unique `(user,message,emoji)`, NO `EventEmitterMixin` since reactions broadcast synchronously not via the outbox). `add_reaction` uses `pg_insert(MessageReaction).on_conflict_do_nothing(index_elements=["user_id","message_id","emoji"])` (idempotent, returns is_new); aggregated via `selectinload(Message.reactions)` + a `_aggregate_reactions(rows, current_user_id)` helper (no N+1). Both `MessageResponse(...)` field-by-field sites must set `reactions`: `get_messages` aggregates, `get_chats` last-message `=[]` (lightweight projection).
- **`MessageDTO.reactions` is a DTO field, not an ORM relationship at the response layer** (W206 SW2/SW3, 2026-05-31). `query_service.get_messages` returns `MessageDTO` (not raw ORM), so reactions flow as `MessageDTO.reactions: list[MessageReactionDTO]` (like attachments), aggregated in `query_service` from the `selectinload`-ed `Message.reactions` rows — NOT exposed via an ORM relationship at the response boundary. REST `MessageResponse.reactions` is `list[ReactionAggregate]{emoji,count,reacted_by_me}` (server-computed `reacted_by_me`).

- **Live typing flips cross-user via a backend REST endpoint, NOT the WS** (W207 SW7/SW8, 2026-05-31). The frontend WS connects to ws-hub, whose `allowedMessageTypes = {join, leave, message}` DROPS `"typing"` at its parse boundary (`services/ws-hub/.../client.go`) — so `sendTyping()` over the socket went nowhere; the fully-built receive `case "typing"` handler (W181) never fired from a real peer. Fix: NEW `POST /chats/{id}/typing` → `ChatMaintenanceService.broadcast_typing` (participant authz via `check_participant` → `raise_forbidden` + `broadcast_to_chat({type:"typing", chat_id, user_id, user_name}, exclude_user_id=user.id)`) → the W204 bridge → ws-hub `chat.*` → the existing receive handler. `sendTyping` is repointed from the dropped WS frame to a throttled (`OUTGOING_RATE_LIMITS.typing` 500ms) `chatApi.sendTyping`; MessageInput `onChange` → `onTyping`. **NO Go change, NO new Go security surface** — the endpoint's `check_participant` IS the send-side membership check. `user_name = getattr(user.profile, "full_name", None) if getattr(user, "profile", None) else str(user.email)` (falls back to the email when the profile is noload). The `dispatcher.py` typing handler is now dead (the frontend uses REST; dedupe later).
- **Reactor-list endpoint: direct User↔MessageReaction join, name/avatar from `UserProfile` not `User`** (W207 SW5, 2026-05-31). `get_reactors(message_id, emoji)` does `select(User).join(MessageReaction, MessageReaction.user_id == User.id).where(...).options(selectinload(User.profile)).order_by(MessageReaction.created_at.asc())` — a DIRECT join, NOT an ORM `MessageReaction.user` relationship (avoids an unused rel). `ReactorOut.name`/`avatar_url` come from `u.profile.full_name`/`u.profile.avatar_url` — **the (z): `User` has NO `full_name`/`avatar_url`** (they live on `UserProfile` via `User.profile`, `lazy="noload"`) → MUST `selectinload(User.profile)` + guard `u.profile.X if u.profile else None`. mypy caught this where the 2949-passing reactor tests would have green-lit it (they mocked `.full_name` directly). GET `/chats/{c}/messages/{m}/reactions?emoji=` coexists with the W206 POST/DELETE at the same path (FastAPI routes by method); reactor identities are fetched on-demand (`enabled: isOpen && !!chatId`), NEVER bundled into `GET /messages` (only the count aggregate is).
- **Reply/quote: self-FK + lean `ReplyPreview` + a `serialize_message` extension for the live frame** (W207 SW1-SW3, 2026-05-31). `Message.reply_to_message_id` self-FK is the canonical adjacency-list `relationship("Message", remote_side="Message.id", lazy="noload")` (single self-FK → `remote_side` alone is unambiguous, no `foreign_keys=[...]`) + `ondelete="SET NULL"` (a reply SURVIVES its target's hard-delete → FE renders "original deleted"). `replied_to` is noload, so the recipient's live `new_message` frame would miss the quote unless `send_message` (a) validates the target via the reused W206 `message_exists_in_chat(reply_to_message_id, chat_id)` EXISTS check (in-chat 404-before-insert — there is NO `get_message_for_reply` method; the EXISTS reuse is cleaner) and (b) loads the relationship via the `selectinload(replied_to)` reads, from which `ReplyPreview.from_message(replied_to)` (`schemas/chat.py:98` — the **lean `{id, sender_id, sender_name, content, deleted_at}`**, NOT a recursive nested `MessageResponse`) is passed into the broadcast's extended `serialize_message(reply_to=...)`. `MessageResponse.reply_to` built at BOTH `get_messages` + `get_chats` last-message sites (W203-SW8 two-site rule). FE Valibot `reply_to: v.optional(v.nullable(...))` (W205 nullable pattern — the backend emits `reply_to: null` when not a reply / target hard-deleted).
- **ReactionPill needs `"use no memo"` (React Compiler Babel transform is stricter than the eslint plugin)** (W207 SW9, 2026-05-31; W199 / FIX-54-01 instance). `frontend/src/components/messenger/ReactionPill.tsx` opens with `"use no memo"` + a paired `// eslint-disable-next-line react-compiler/react-compiler` (the plugin calls the directive "unused"; the Babel transform NEEDS it). floating-ui's `getReferenceProps({onClick,...})` ref-merging + the imperative long-press refs trip `validateNoRefAccessInRender` ("Cannot access refs during render") at `@rolldown/plugin-babel` BUILD time even though the refs are only touched in handlers. **The build is the gate that catches this** — SW6's tsc + eslint + vitest ALL passed; only `npm run build` (Build × 3) failed. Lesson: when a component merges floating-ui interaction props or touches refs in render-adjacent closures, expect the Babel transform to disagree with eslint — `"use no memo"` is the fix.
- **Scroll-threshold FAB visibility MUST be state-driven, never ref-in-render** (W208 SW4, 2026-06-01; W199 / W207 SW9 ReactionPill instance class). The scroll-to-bottom FAB in `ChatWindow.tsx` derives visibility from `useState` (read in render); it reads `containerRef.current`'s scroll metrics ONLY inside the `{ passive: true }` scroll-listener handler (a ref read in a handler is fine; a ref read DURING render trips `@rolldown/plugin-babel`'s `validateNoRefAccessInRender` at `npm run build`, which eslint does NOT catch). The FAB passed Build × 3 WITHOUT `"use no memo"` precisely because of this discipline — the same pattern as `animateFromIndex` (W202 SW6b). Pattern recipe for any "show X past a scroll threshold" UI: `const [show, setShow] = useState(false)` + a scroll listener that computes the metric and calls `setShow(...)` in the handler; the scroll `<div>` wrapped in `relative flex flex-1 min-h-0 flex-col` so the FAB is an `absolute` sibling without breaking the `flex-1 min-h-0 overflow-y-auto` virtualizer-height chain.
- **Date dividers + sender grouping are row ANNOTATIONS, never separate virtual rows** (W208 SW5, 2026-06-01). In the `@tanstack/react-virtual` message list, per-day dividers are annotation fields (`showDateDivider`/`dateLabel`) + grouping is `isGroupStart` — all OPTIONAL on `Message` (so the optimistic builder is untouched), computed in `useMessengerController`'s `transformedMessages` useMemo (`(m, i) =>` with `prev = messages[i-1]`). ChatWindow renders the divider INSIDE the existing positioned `measureElement` virtual item (above the bubble); `estimateSize` auto-measures the extra height and `count: filteredMessages.length` stays unchanged → the W184 SW1 `filteredMessages[virtualRow.index]` count↔index alignment is preserved. NEVER add a separate virtual row for a divider (it desyncs the index). For grouping, swap the avatar for an `aria-hidden` same-dimension spacer when `isGroupStart === false` (undefined keeps the avatar) — never collapse the row. **Locale gotcha:** the absolute `dateLabel` MUST pass `i18n.language` to `formatDate(m.created_at, presets.chatGroup, locale)` — do NOT mirror `formatMessageTime`'s locale-less call (it's always en-US). `now`/`yesterdayStart` are per-render snapshots, intentionally NOT in the memo deps (adding them defeats memoization).
- **`chat.reply` supersede excludes the quoted author from the generic `chat.message`** (W208 SW1, 2026-06-01). `ChatNotificationService.notify_new_message` — when X replies to Y's message (`is_reply_to_other = replied is not None and replied.sender_id != sender.id`), Y is REMOVED from the generic `chat.message` recipient list + gets a single specific `chat.reply` (`tag=chat-reply:{replied.id}`, `dedupe_key=chat-reply:{message.id}` idempotent, str-wrapped `payload_data`) — no double-notify. Use `replied.sender_id` (it's a `MessageDTO` — there is NO `.sender.id`). In a 2-person DM the generic list empties after the exclusion, so the shared `sender_name`/`body_preview` + the reply send must be guarded by `if other_participants or is_reply_to_other:` (else the lone DM recipient gets NO notification). The live WS `new_message` frame is UNTOUCHED — only the persistent bell/push entry upgrades from generic to specific, so the **FE needs zero changes** (NotificationsBell renders generically by `type`; no new FE i18n key). A self-reply (`replied.sender_id == sender.id`) or a hard-deleted target (`reply_to_message_id` → NULL → `replied is None`) keeps the generic-only path.
